food_culture.name: Gahwa (Arabic coffee)
food_culture.description: Lightly roasted, brewed with cardamom, and poured from a dallah pot into small handle-less cups — refusing the first cup is traditionally seen as declining hospitality. UNESCO-recognized Intangible Cultural Heritage since 2015.

food_culture.name: Machboos
food_culture.description: The UAE's national dish — fragrant spiced rice with chicken, lamb, or seafood, infused with dried lime (loomi) for a tangy depth.

food_culture.name: Karak tea

food_culture.name: Luqaimat & kunafa
food_culture.description: Luqaimat are sweet fried dumplings drizzled with date syrup; kunafa is a cheese-and-syrup pastry dessert popular across the Gulf and Levant.

food_culture.name: Al Fahidi Cultural Understanding Centre
food_culture.description: A government-run center in Old Dubai offering meals and cultural sessions specifically designed to teach visitors authentic Emirati customs and Bedouin heritage, beyond the skyline.

food_culture.name: Nyepi (Day of Silence)
food_culture.description: The Balinese Hindu New Year, marked not with celebration but a full day of island-wide silence — airports close, roads empty, and lights go off. Visitors are expected to observe the same restrictions.

food_culture.name: Babi Guling
food_culture.description: Balinese spit-roasted suckling pig, originally a sacred temple offering — pork is central to Bali's food identity, distinguishing it from the rest of Muslim-majority Indonesia.

food_culture.name: Bebek Betutu
food_culture.description: Duck or chicken slow-cooked in banana leaves with a rich spice marinade, traditionally served at Hindu ceremonies — often requires ordering a day in advance.

food_culture.name: Canang sari offerings
food_culture.description: Small daily woven-palm offerings of flowers and food left outside homes and businesses to honor the gods — a visible, constant part of Balinese Hindu life.

food_culture.name: Base genep
food_culture.description: Bali's foundational spice paste — garlic, turmeric, ginger, galangal, lemongrass, and chili ground together — underlying most traditional dishes on the island.

food_culture.name: Mas riha (Maldivian tuna curry)
food_culture.description: A coconut-based curry built on tuna rather than chicken or lamb, since fishing — not agriculture — has always defined the Maldivian diet.

food_culture.name: Hedhikaa (short eats)
food_culture.description: Maldivian tea-time snacks like bajiya (fried tuna-and-coconut pastries) and gulha (fish balls) — direct relatives of Indian samosas and Sri Lankan cutlets, served the same way at teatime.

food_culture.name: Ceylon tea
food_culture.description: Sri Lanka is one of the world's great tea producers — a plantation tour near Kandy showing the withering, rolling, and fermenting process is a genuine highlight if extending into Sri Lanka.

food_culture.name: Kiribath & watalappam
food_culture.description: Sri Lankan milk rice (kiribath) is the celebratory dish for New Year and auspicious occasions; watalappam, a coconut-jaggery custard, reflects the island's Malay community influence.

food_culture.name: Spice gardens of Matale
food_culture.description: Sri Lanka's spices — cinnamon, cardamom, pepper, nutmeg — are grown here and were historically believed to have medicinal as well as flavoring value, not just culinary ones.

food_culture.name: Turkish tea (çay)
food_culture.description: Served in small tulip-shaped glasses, strong and without milk — offered constantly as a gesture of hospitality, and refusing it is considered impolite.

food_culture.name: Turkish coffee & fortune telling
food_culture.description: Slow-brewed and unfiltered, traditionally followed by a fortune-teller (falcı) reading the pattern left by the grounds in the empty cup — a genuine social ritual, not just a novelty.

food_culture.name: Regional cuisine variety
food_culture.description: Turkish food shifts by region — olive-oil vegetable dishes on the Aegean coast, fresh fish in Bodrum, baklava-heavy pastry culture in the east, hearty wheat-and-meat stews (keşkek) in central Anatolia.

food_culture.name: Turkish hospitality (misafirperverlik)
food_culture.description: Guests are offered food and drink almost immediately upon arrival anywhere — home, shop, or hotel — and the phrase 'hoş geldiniz' ('it's good you came') captures a genuinely central cultural value.

food_culture.name: Whirling dervish ceremony
food_culture.description: A Sufi religious ritual (sema) especially associated with Konya — meditative spinning dance representing spiritual ascent, still performed as a living tradition, not just a tourist show.

food_culture.name: Pura Vida
food_culture.description: Literally 'pure life' — more than a greeting, it's a whole philosophy of living simply, gratefully, and in the moment that genuinely shapes the pace of daily life.

food_culture.name: Gallo pinto
food_culture.description: Costa Rica's everyday breakfast — rice and black beans sautéed with Salsa Lizano, a tangy brown sauce found on nearly every table in the country.

food_culture.name: Casado
food_culture.description: The classic Costa Rican lunch plate — rice, beans, plantains, salad, and a choice of protein — named for resembling 'what my wife would make.'

food_culture.name: Costa Rican coffee
food_culture.description: Grown in the misty Central Valley highlands and traditionally brewed through a cloth chorreador filter — genuinely high-quality, and a point of national pride.

food_culture.name: Sodas

food_culture.name: The Georgian supra
food_culture.description: A ceremonial feast that can run for hours, led by a tamada (toastmaster) whose toasts — to family, guests, ancestors, and peace — set the rhythm of the entire meal. An empty table is considered shameful.

food_culture.name: Khachapuri & khinkali
food_culture.description: Khachapuri is Georgia's cheese-filled bread, with a dozen regional varieties (the boat-shaped Adjarian version topped with a raw egg is the most photographed); khinkali are pleated dumplings eaten by the knob, which is traditionally left uneaten.

food_culture.name: Qvevri wine
food_culture.description: Georgia calls itself the cradle of viticulture — evidence at Gadachrili Gora suggests winemaking here 8,000 years ago, still using the same qvevri clay-vessel fermentation method.

food_culture.name: Lavash & khorovats
food_culture.description: Armenia's UNESCO-protected paper-thin flatbread, baked in a clay tonir oven, is the universal utensil for wrapping khorovats — Armenian charcoal-grilled meat skewers.

food_culture.name: Dolma
food_culture.description: Grape leaves or vegetables stuffed with spiced meat and rice — claimed by Armenia as a national dish, though variations of it appear across the Caucasus, Balkans, and Levant.

food_culture.name: Arepa
food_culture.description: A simple maize flatbread that varies by region — thin and plain in Bogotá, cheese-stuffed and fried in Cartagena, sweetened in Medellín — found at every meal, on every street corner.

food_culture.name: Bandeja paisa

food_culture.name: Colombian coffee culture

food_culture.name: Coastal ceviche

food_culture.name: Ceviche
food_culture.description: Peru's national dish and a UNESCO-recognized piece of intangible cultural heritage since 2004 — raw fish cured in lime with chili and onion, at its best in Lima but found nationwide.

food_culture.name: Pisco sour
food_culture.description: Peru's national cocktail — pisco brandy, lime juice, syrup, and egg white — a genuine point of pride and rivalry with Chile, which also claims pisco as its own.

food_culture.name: Lomo saltado
food_culture.description: A stir-fried beef dish with soy sauce and french fries, reflecting Peru's significant Chinese (chifa) immigrant influence on everyday cooking.

food_culture.name: Cuy (guinea pig)
food_culture.description: A traditional Andean dish, especially associated with the Cusco region — crispy skin, tender meat, served with native potatoes. A genuinely adventurous try for most visitors.

food_culture.name: Aji de gallina
food_culture.description: Shredded chicken in a creamy sauce built on ají amarillo, a native yellow chili with fruity heat rather than sharp spice — a signature dish of the Andean highlands.

food_culture.name: Adobo
food_culture.description: Meat slow-stewed in vinegar, soy sauce, garlic, and peppercorns — the Philippines' most iconic dish, with every family keeping its own version.

food_culture.name: Fiesta & lechon
food_culture.description: Every town holds its own fiesta honoring a patron saint, centered on lechon — a whole roasted pig, spit-roasted for hours, that functions as a genuine symbol of abundance and community.

food_culture.name: Bayanihan

food_culture.name: Kamayan
food_culture.description: Eating with bare hands directly off banana leaves, shared family-style — a tradition that emphasizes the communal, connective role food plays in Filipino life.

food_culture.name: Sinigang
food_culture.description: A sour tamarind-based soup loaded with vegetables and meat or seafood — considered the ultimate Filipino comfort food.

food_culture.name: Rakija
food_culture.description: Serbia's fruit brandy — plum (šljivovica) is the most common — offered as a welcome drink to any guest and central to nearly every celebration.

food_culture.name: Slava

food_culture.name: Meze & ajvar

food_culture.name: Kafana coffee culture

food_culture.name: Pasulj & punjena paprika

food_culture.name: Hanal Pixán

food_culture.name: Pan de muerto

food_culture.name: Mexico City street food

food_culture.name: Mezcal & tequila regions

Fort Ransom State Park in the wooded Sheyenne Valley

title: Cleveland & Cuyahoga Valley National Park
best_time_description: Fall brings foliage color along the Cuyahoga Valley's gorges, while late spring through summer keeps the Cuyahoga Valley Scenic Railroad and full trail network running.
description: A northern Ohio pairing of Cleveland's lakefront museums with the waterfalls, ledges, and scenic railroad of Cuyahoga Valley National Park, distinct from Hocking Hills in the state's south.

Great Lakes Science Center and its NASA Glenn Visitor Center

Playhouse Square's restored 1920s theater district

days.title: Cuyahoga Valley National Park

Bike or walk a stretch of the Ohio & Erie Canal Towpath Trail

title: Wichita Mountains & Oklahoma's Route 66
best_time_description: Spring and fall bring mild temperatures for hiking and driving; June is calving season for the refuge's bison and longhorn herds. Wichita Mountains hiking trails close to foot traffic after 10 a.m.
description: A western Oklahoma road trip along the Mother Road's roadside icons, ending in the granite peaks and free-roaming bison of the Wichita Mountains, distinct from the Tulsa/Turner Falls/OKC route.

Onion burger lunch in El Reno, birthplace of the fried onion burger
Oklahoma Route 66 Museum in Clinton

Additional refuge hiking or a visit to the Holy City of the Wichitas

title: Oregon Coast: Cannon Beach to Bandon
best_time_description: Late March through May brings the northbound gray whale migration and thinner crowds; summer has the warmest, driest beach weather, though fog and wind are common on this coast year-round.
description: A full Highway 101 run down the Oregon coast from Haystack Rock to the sea stacks of Bandon, a separate coastal itinerary from the state's inland Columbia River Gorge route.

Ecola State Park viewpoint over the coastline

days.title: Cannon Beach to Newport

Yaquina Head Lighthouse and tide pools in Newport
Watch sea lions on the docks near the Yaquina Bay Bridge

days.title: Newport to Florence

Walk the dunes at Oregon Dunes National Recreation Area

days.title: Florence to Bandon

Face Rock State Scenic Viewpoint

Bullards Beach State Park and the Coquille River lighthouse
Wildlife and seasonal whale watching from Coquille Point

title: Tokyo, Kyoto + Osaka, Japan
best_time_description: Spring (late March to mid-April) brings cherry blossoms in Tokyo and Kyoto, while autumn (mid-October to late November) brings fiery maple foliage in both cities — the two most comfortable and scenic windows, though also the most crowded and expensive for lodging.
description: Tokyo's neon-lit modernity, then the temples, torii gates, and old wooden streets of Kyoto, with a day trip into Osaka's food-obsessed downtown — Japan's classic first-timer arc, connected by the Shinkansen bullet train.

days.title: Arrive Tokyo
activities: Narita Express (N'EX) from Narita Airport to Tokyo Station, about 53-60 minutes
Settle into Shinjuku or Shibuya
Evening walk through Shinjuku's Omoide Yokocho alleys

days.title: Old Tokyo
activities: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise shopping street in Asakusa
Tokyo Skytree observation deck
Sumida River walk

days.title: Modern Tokyo
activities: Shibuya Scramble Crossing and Shibuya Sky observation deck
Harajuku's Takeshita Street and Meiji Shrine
Shopping and dinner in Ginza

days.title: Tsukiji + travel to Kyoto
activities: Early morning at Tsukiji Outer Market for fresh seafood breakfast
Shinkansen (Nozomi) from Tokyo Station to Kyoto Station, about 2 hours 15 minutes
Evening stroll through Gion's lantern-lit lanes

days.title: Kyoto shrines and temples
activities: Fushimi Inari Taisha and its thousands of vermilion torii gates
Kiyomizu-dera Temple and the Higashiyama district's preserved streets
Evening in Pontocho Alley

days.title: Arashiyama + northern Kyoto
activities: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove at opening time to beat the crowds
Tenryu-ji Temple garden
Kinkaku-ji (the Golden Pavilion)

days.title: Osaka day trip
activities: JR Special Rapid train from Kyoto Station to Osaka Station, about 28 minutes
Osaka Castle and its surrounding park
Dotonbori's neon signs, takoyaki, and okonomiyaki
Return to Kyoto, or continue to Kansai Airport for a flight home
days.drive_time: JR Special Rapid, ~28 min each way

days.title: Optional: Nara side trip or departure
activities: Optional day trip to Nara Park to see the free-roaming sika deer and Todai-ji Temple (JR Nara Line, about 45 minutes from Kyoto Station)
Depart from Kansai International Airport (KIX) or return to Tokyo for a flight home
days.drive_time: JR Nara Line, ~45 min each way (optional day)

food_culture.name: Sushi and Tsukiji-style seafood breakfast
food_culture.description: Tokyo's Tsukiji Outer Market (the old wholesale fish market's surviving retail street, after the wholesale auctions moved to Toyosu in 2018) is packed with stalls serving fresh sushi, grilled seafood skewers, and tamagoyaki for breakfast.

food_culture.name: Kaiseki
food_culture.description: Kyoto's refined multi-course kaiseki cuisine grew out of the tea ceremony's meal traditions, emphasizing seasonal ingredients and careful presentation — a contrast to Osaka's more casual street food culture.

food_culture.name: Takoyaki and okonomiyaki
food_culture.description: Osaka calls itself the nation's kitchen ("tenka no daidokoro") and is famous for takoyaki (octopus-filled batter balls) and okonomiyaki (savory grilled cabbage pancakes) sold throughout Dotonbori.

food_culture.name: Matcha and tea ceremony culture
food_culture.description: Kyoto, especially nearby Uji, is one of Japan's historic centers of matcha production, and traditional tea houses around the city offer formal tea ceremony experiences rooted in centuries-old ritual.

food_culture.name: Izakaya culture
food_culture.description: After-work izakaya (casual pubs serving small plates and drinks) are central to Tokyo's social life, clustered densely in alleys like Shinjuku's Omoide Yokocho and under railway arches near major stations.

food_culture.name: Torii gate pilgrimage paths
food_culture.description: Fushimi Inari Taisha's roughly 10,000 vermilion torii gates, donated by individuals and businesses over centuries, form pilgrimage trails up Mount Inari dedicated to the Shinto rice deity Inari.

title: Bangkok + Chiang Mai, Thailand
best_time_description: November to February is Thailand's cool, dry season — the most comfortable window for temple-hopping in Bangkok's heat and for hiking around Chiang Mai, where northern evenings can turn genuinely chilly.
description: Bangkok's riverside temples and market chaos, then a short flight north to Chiang Mai's walled Old City, mountain temples, and an ethical elephant sanctuary — Thailand's two most iconic and easiest-to-combine regions.

days.title: Arrive Bangkok
activities: Settle in near the Chao Phraya riverside
Evening river cruise past illuminated Wat Arun

days.title: Bangkok temples
activities: Grand Palace and Wat Phra Kaew (Temple of the Emerald Buddha)
Wat Pho's reclining Buddha and traditional Thai massage school
Cross the river to climb Wat Arun's central prang

days.title: Ayutthaya day trip
activities: Train or van to the ruined former capital, Ayutthaya
Wat Mahathat's tree-entwined Buddha head and Wat Chaiwatthanaram's Khmer-style ruins
Return to Bangkok by evening

days.title: Bangkok markets + fly to Chiang Mai
activities: Morning at Chatuchak Weekend Market (if a weekend) or Talad Rot Fai night market
Afternoon flight to Chiang Mai (about 1 hour 15 minutes)
Evening walk through Chiang Mai's walled Old City

days.title: Chiang Mai Old City + Doi Suthep
activities: Wat Phra Singh and Wat Chedi Luang inside the Old City walls
Drive up to Wat Phra That Doi Suthep, the gold-spired mountain temple overlooking the city
Sunday Walking Street night market (if timing allows) or the Chiang Mai Night Bazaar
days.drive_time: 30 to 40 min each way to Doi Suthep

days.title: Elephant Nature Park
activities: Full-day visit to Elephant Nature Park, an observation-only rescued-elephant sanctuary with no riding or bathing
Help prepare food for the elephants and watch them from the riverside observation area

days.title: Doi Inthanon National Park
activities: Day trip to Doi Inthanon, Thailand's highest peak
Wachirathan and Siriphum waterfalls, twin royal chedis, and hill-tribe market stalls

days.title: Departure
activities: Last-minute shopping for northern Thai handicrafts at a local market
Fly home from Chiang Mai or connect back through Bangkok

food_culture.name: Khao soi
food_culture.description: Chiang Mai's signature dish: curried coconut broth with egg noodles, topped with crispy fried noodles — a northern Thai specialty rarely found in the same form in Bangkok.

food_culture.name: Pad thai and boat noodles
food_culture.description: Bangkok street-food staples — stir-fried rice noodles with tamarind, egg, and shrimp, and intensely flavored boat noodle soup traditionally sold from canal-side boats.

food_culture.name: Thai iced tea (cha yen)
food_culture.description: Strongly brewed black tea sweetened with condensed milk, served over ice — a ubiquitous street-stall drink across both cities.

food_culture.name: Wai greeting
food_culture.description: The traditional Thai greeting — palms pressed together at chest or forehead height with a slight bow — used as both hello and thank-you, and expected as a sign of respect when entering temples.

food_culture.name: Lanna heritage of Chiang Mai
food_culture.description: Chiang Mai was capital of the independent Lanna kingdom until the late 1800s, giving it a distinct northern Thai architecture, dialect, and temple style still visible in the Old City's walls and moat.

title: Hanoi, Ha Long Bay + Ninh Binh, Vietnam
best_time_description: October–November and March–April are the sweet spots for northern Vietnam: the dry season (roughly November–April) keeps rainfall low, but December–February can be gray and chilly (down to the mid-teens Celsius) while May–October brings the southwest monsoon's heaviest rain and occasional typhoons that can cancel Ha Long Bay cruises.
description: Hanoi's Old Quarter chaos, a limestone-karst boat glide through Ninh Binh's Trang An wetlands, and an overnight cruise among the towering islets of Ha Long Bay — the classic northern Vietnam loop, all within a few hours of the capital.

days.title: Arrive Hanoi
activities: Settle into the Old Quarter
Evening walk around Hoan Kiem Lake and Ngoc Son Temple
First bowl of pho at a street-side quan

days.title: Hanoi's imperial and colonial layers
activities: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex and the One Pillar Pagoda
Temple of Literature, Vietnam's first national university
Walk the tracks at Train Street
Evening water puppet show at Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre

days.title: Ninh Binh day trip: Trang An and Mua Cave
activities: Sampan boat tour through the Trang An Landscape Complex's limestone karsts and river caves
Climb the roughly 500 steps to the Mua Cave viewpoint over the Tam Coc rice paddies
Return to Hanoi by early evening

days.title: Transfer to Ha Long Bay, board overnight cruise
activities: Morning transfer from Hanoi to the Ha Long Bay pier
Board an overnight junk-style cruise among the bay's limestone islets
Kayak or bamboo-boat into Luon Cave
Sunset on the sundeck
days.lodging_suggestion: Overnight cruise boat, Ha Long Bay

days.title: Ha Long Bay caves and islands, back to Hanoi
activities: Morning visit to Sung Sot (Surprise) Cave
Swim or climb for the panoramic view at Ti Top Island
Disembark and transfer back to Hanoi by evening

days.title: Hanoi crafts and coffee culture
activities: Ferry or bridge crossing to Bat Trang ceramic village to watch potters at work
Egg coffee (ca phe trung) at Cafe Giang, the Old Quarter cafe that invented it in 1946
Wander the 36 Streets of the Old Quarter, each still loosely tied to its historic guild trade

days.title: Depart Hanoi
activities: Last-minute shopping for lacquerware or silk on Hang Gai street
Transfer to Noi Bai International Airport

food_culture.name: Pho
food_culture.description: Northern Vietnam's clear, delicate beef or chicken noodle soup, believed to have emerged in the Red River Delta region around Hanoi in the early 20th century and still eaten at breakfast as much as any other meal.

food_culture.name: Bun cha
food_culture.description: Grilled pork patties and belly served in a sweet-tangy fish-sauce broth over rice vermicelli — a Hanoi specialty that gained global attention after Anthony Bourdain and Barack Obama shared a meal of it at a Hanoi restaurant in 2016.

food_culture.name: Ca phe trung (egg coffee)
food_culture.description: A thick froth of whisked egg yolk, sugar, and condensed milk over hot coffee, invented in 1946 by Nguyen Van Giang during a wartime milk shortage; his family's Cafe Giang in the Old Quarter still serves it.

food_culture.name: Water puppetry (mua roi nuoc)
food_culture.description: An art form dating to 11th-century rice-farming villages in the Red River Delta, where puppeteers stood waist-deep in flooded paddies to work wooden figures on rods; Hanoi's Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre performs it nightly for visitors.

food_culture.name: The 36 Streets of the Old Quarter
food_culture.description: Hanoi's Old Quarter grew from craft guilds that settled near the royal citadel starting in the 11th century, each given a street named for its trade with the prefix "Hang" — Hang Bac (silver), Hang Gai (silk), Hang Ma (votive paper) — a layout still visible today.

title: Cairo, Abu Simbel + Nile Cruise, Egypt
best_time_description: October through April is Egypt's comfortable season, with mild daytime temperatures and cool nights across both Cairo and Upper Egypt. February and March are the sweet spot for the Aswan/Luxor leg — warm and sunny without the brutal summer heat of the south — while December and January are the busiest and most expensive weeks on the Nile.
description: Pyramids and museum treasures in Cairo, a desert dawn run to Abu Simbel, then four days drifting up the Nile by cruise ship through Kom Ombo and Edfu to Luxor's Valley of the Kings — Egypt's classic first-timer route, hitting all three geographic zones (Cairo, Upper Egypt by air, the Nile itself by boat) in one real, commonly-run itinerary.

days.title: Arrive Cairo
activities: Settle in near Giza or downtown Cairo
Evening stroll along the Nile Corniche

days.title: Giza Plateau
activities: Great Pyramids of Giza and the Sphinx
Solar Boat Museum
Optional camel or horseback ride around the plateau

days.title: Cairo city
activities: Egyptian Museum in Tahrir Square
Khan el-Khalili bazaar
Islamic Cairo: Sultan Hassan Mosque and Al-Azhar

days.title: Cairo → Aswan (fly)
activities: Morning EgyptAir flight Cairo to Aswan (about 1 hr 25 min)
Philae Temple by boat
Aswan High Dam
Sunset felucca sail past Elephantine Island

activities: Pre-dawn departure for the temples of Abu Simbel
Great Temple of Ramses II and the Temple of Hathor/Nefertari
Return to Aswan by mid-afternoon

days.title: Board Nile cruise: Aswan → Kom Ombo → Edfu
activities: Board Nile cruise ship in Aswan
Sail to Kom Ombo, visit the twin temple of Sobek and Horus
Continue overnight toward Edfu

days.title: Edfu → Esna → Luxor
activities: Horse-drawn carriage to the Temple of Horus at Edfu
Sail through the Esna lock
Arrive Luxor; sunset felucca or free evening

days.title: Luxor and depart
activities: Valley of the Kings and the Temple of Hatshepsut on the West Bank
Karnak Temple and Luxor Temple
Fly Luxor → Cairo for onward departure

food_culture.name: Koshari
food_culture.description: Widely considered Egypt's national dish: a hearty layered mix of rice, lentils, macaroni and chickpeas, topped with a spiced tomato sauce and crispy fried onions. It arrived in Egypt with 19th-century Indian influence but is now the country's defining street food.

food_culture.name: Ful wi ta'ameya
food_culture.description: Egypt's classic breakfast duo — ful medames (stewed, mashed fava beans) alongside ta'ameya, Egypt's own fava-bean version of falafel (as opposed to the chickpea falafel found elsewhere in the region), both with roots going back millennia.

food_culture.name: Karkade (hibiscus tea)
food_culture.description: A deep-red, tart infusion of dried hibiscus petals, served hot or iced. Upper Egypt around Aswan and Qena is one of the country's main hibiscus-growing regions, so karkade is especially associated with the Aswan leg of a Nile trip.

food_culture.name: Felucca sailing on the Nile
food_culture.description: The felucca is a traditional wide-sailed wooden boat, unchanged in basic design since Pharaonic times, still used around Aswan and Luxor for sunset sails and short crossings to river islands and Nubian villages.

food_culture.name: Nubian culture around Aswan
food_culture.description: The Nubian people, whose roots trace back over 4,000 years to ancient kingdoms south of Egypt, live along the Nile around Aswan in villages known for brightly painted homes; many were relocated here after the High Dam's construction flooded their original settlements in the 1960s.

title: Marrakech & the Sahara Desert, Morocco
best_time_description: Spring (March to May) and fall (September to November) hit the sweet spot for this route: warm, comfortable days in Marrakech and the High Atlas without the Sahara's brutal mid-summer heat (daytime temps regularly top 45C/113F in Merzouga from June to August, and some desert camps scale back). October and November are especially good for the desert leg — clear skies, cooler nights, and better stargazing at the camp.
description: A classic loop from Marrakech's medina over the High Atlas Mountains to the dunes of the Sahara — the kasbah of Ait Benhaddou, the Dades Valley, and a camel trek into Erg Chebbi to sleep under the stars, before looping back through Ouarzazate's film studios.

days.title: Arrive Marrakech
activities: Settle into a riad in the Medina
Evening at Jemaa el-Fnaa — food stalls, snake charmers, and storytellers as the square comes alive after dark

days.title: Marrakech city day
activities: Bahia Palace and the Saadian Tombs
Majorelle Garden and the Yves Saint Laurent Museum
Wander the souks of the Medina

days.title: Over the High Atlas to the Dades Valley
activities: Cross the High Atlas via the Tizi n'Tichka Pass (2,260m)
Explore the UNESCO-listed kasbah of Ait Benhaddou
Continue into the Dades Valley, the 'Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs'
days.drive_time: ~7 hrs total (Marrakech to Ait Benhaddou ~3-4 hrs; Ait Benhaddou to Dades Valley ~3 hrs)

days.title: Todra Gorge to the Sahara
activities: Stop at Todra Gorge, a narrow limestone canyon popular with rock climbers
Drive on to Merzouga at the edge of Erg Chebbi
Camel trek into the dunes for sunset and an overnight stay at a desert camp
days.drive_time: ~4-5 hrs (Dades Valley to Merzouga via Tinghir/Todra Gorge)

days.title: Sahara sunrise to Ouarzazate
activities: Sunrise over the dunes, camel ride back to Merzouga
Drive back across the Dades Valley to Ouarzazate
Visit Ouarzazate's Atlas Film Studios and the Taourirt Kasbah

days.title: Back to Marrakech
activities: Cross the Tizi n'Tichka Pass back to Marrakech
Afternoon at a traditional hammam to unwind after the road trip

days.title: Depart Marrakech
activities: Last-minute shopping in the souks for lanterns, leather, and spices
Fly home

food_culture.name: Tagine
food_culture.description: A slow-cooked stew named for the conical clay pot it simmers in — chicken with preserved lemon and olives, or lamb with prunes and almonds, are two of the most common versions found from Marrakech to the desert.

food_culture.name: Couscous
food_culture.description: Traditionally served on Fridays after communal prayers, steamed semolina piled with seven vegetables and meat — a weekly family ritual as much as a dish.

food_culture.name: Moroccan mint tea (atay)
food_culture.description: Green tea brewed with fresh spearmint and sugar, poured from a height to build a froth on top; offering three rounds of tea is a core hospitality ritual across the country, from riads to Berber tents.

food_culture.name: Berber desert camps of Erg Chebbi
food_culture.description: Berber guides lead camel treks into the dunes around Merzouga for sunset and sunrise, with communal drumming and singing around the fire at the camp afterward — a tradition rooted in the region's nomadic trading routes across the Sahara.

food_culture.name: Hammam
food_culture.description: The traditional steam bathhouse, found in nearly every neighborhood, where a black-soap scrub and communal bathing are a weekly ritual rather than a spa indulgence — many riads in Marrakech offer a version for visitors.

title: Paris + Loire Valley Châteaux, France
best_time_description: Late spring and early autumn are comfortable for walking Paris and the Loire château grounds and are outside the peak summer crowds; this is an editorial suggestion rather than met-service data. Check opening days for the Louvre (closed Tuesdays) and Versailles (closed Mondays) when ordering the days.
description: France's classic first-timer arc: four days in Paris including a Versailles day trip, then a fast TGV to Tours as a base for the Loire châteaux of Amboise and Chenonceau, all reachable by train without a car.

days.title: Arrive Paris
activities: Check in and walk the Seine embankments toward Île de la Cité
Evening in the Latin Quarter or Le Marais

days.title: Louvre + the Tuileries
activities: Louvre Museum: book a timeslot on the official louvre.fr site before you go (timeslot booking is recommended, and reservations have been compulsory for all visitors in some periods, so check the dates for your trip). Closed Tuesdays, 1 January, 1 May and 25 December.
Walk the Tuileries Garden toward Place de la Concorde
Evening stroll along the Seine

days.title: Palace of Versailles day trip
activities: RER line C from central Paris to Versailles Château Rive Gauche, the station closest to the Palace (about a 10-minute walk); the RER C has been closed for works in some summers, so check before you travel
Palace of Versailles, open every day except Monday: buy a timed-entry ticket only from the official Château de Versailles ticket office, and arrive at opening on busy days
Gardens and the Grand Canal
Return to Paris for the evening
days.drive_time: RER C from central Paris (check the timetable on the day)

days.title: Eiffel Tower + Montmartre
activities: Eiffel Tower: buy tickets only on the official ticket.toureiffel.paris site, where timed tickets can be booked in advance; the official site says elevator tickets open up to 90 days ahead
Trocadéro viewpoint and the Champ de Mars
Montmartre: Sacré-Cœur and the streets around Place du Tertre

days.title: TGV to Tours
activities: TGV from Paris Montparnasse to Tours, about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes depending on the train (Tours tourist office lists 25 TGV connections a day); note that the high-speed station Saint-Pierre-des-Corps is 5 minutes from Tours
Place Plumereau and the old town
Tours Cathedral (Cathédrale Saint-Gatien)
days.drive_time: TGV Paris Montparnasse to Tours, ~1 hr to 1 hr 15
days.lodging_suggestion: Tours (old town or near Tours station)

days.title: Amboise
activities: TER from Tours to Amboise, about 20 minutes (SNCF Connect lists direct TER journeys of 19 to 22 minutes)
Château royal d'Amboise above the Loire
Clos Lucé, where Leonardo da Vinci spent his last years
Return to Tours by TER
days.drive_time: TER Tours to Amboise, ~20 min each way
days.lodging_suggestion: Tours (old town or near Tours station)

days.title: Chenonceau
activities: TER from Tours to Chenonceaux, about 25 minutes (SNCF Connect lists 24 to 27 minutes, and only about 10 trains a day, so check the timetable for your outbound and return times); the station is about 400 m from the ticket office
Château de Chenonceau spanning the Cher: the château advises booking tickets online
Return to Tours by TER
days.drive_time: TER Tours to Chenonceaux, ~25 min each way
days.lodging_suggestion: Tours (old town or near Tours station)

days.title: Optional: return to Paris + depart
activities: TGV from Tours to Paris Montparnasse, about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes depending on the train
Depart from Paris
days.drive_time: TGV Tours to Paris Montparnasse, ~1 hr to 1 hr 15
days.lodging_suggestion: Paris (near your departure station or airport)

food_culture.name: The baguette
food_culture.description: The craftsmanship and culture of the baguette de pain was inscribed by UNESCO on its intangible cultural heritage list in 2022; a boulangerie breakfast is a daily Paris ritual.

food_culture.name: The gastronomic meal of the French
food_culture.description: UNESCO recognises the gastronomic meal of the French (inscribed 2010) as intangible heritage: a social custom of celebrating moments with a structured, shared meal.

food_culture.name: Loire Valley wines
food_culture.description: Touraine, around Tours and Amboise, is a Loire wine region; Vouvray and Chinon are well-known names from the area and are easy to find in Tours restaurants and caves.

food_culture.name: Sainte-Maure de Touraine goat cheese
food_culture.description: A goat cheese from the Touraine area with a protected designation of origin, recognisable by the straw running through its centre.

food_culture.name: Café terrace culture
food_culture.description: Sitting for an hour over a coffee on a Paris café terrace, and ordering the daily 'plat du jour' at lunch, are ordinary parts of the local rhythm rather than tourist rituals.

title: Provence + the French Riviera, France
best_time_description: Late spring and early autumn are comfortable for walking in Avignon, Marseille and Nice and fall outside the peak summer crowds; this is an editorial suggestion. Summer brings fire-risk rules in the Calanques (see Day 4), so check access before planning a hike.
description: A south-of-France route by train: Avignon's papal city, Marseille and the Calanques, then Nice and a day trip to Monaco, using TGV and regional trains with no car needed.

days.title: Arrive Avignon
activities: TGV from Paris Gare de Lyon to Avignon TGV station, about 2 hr 40 (Avignon tourist office); the TGV station is about 6 km from the centre, linked to Avignon Centre station by a few-minute TER ride
Walk the ramparts and old town
Pont Saint-Bénézet (the Pont d'Avignon) at sunset

days.title: Palais des Papes + the Luberon
activities: Palais des Papes: check ticketing and opening days on the official site before you go
Rocher des Doms park above the Rhône
Afternoon: Roussillon and Gordes in the Luberon are reached by bus or guided excursion, not by train (per the Avignon tourist office), so book a guided excursion or arrange a car

days.title: Avignon to Marseille
activities: Train from Avignon to Marseille Saint-Charles: journey times vary by train (SNCF Connect lists direct trains from Avignon Centre at roughly 50 minutes to 2 hours, averaging about 1 hr 26), so check the timetable for your day; the TGV station is about 5 minutes from Avignon Centre by TER shuttle
Vieux-Port and the Le Panier quarter
MuCEM and the Fort Saint-Jean waterfront
Notre-Dame de la Garde basilica for the harbour views
days.drive_time: Train Avignon to Marseille, ~1 hr 30 on average (check SNCF Connect)

days.title: Calanques
activities: Parc national des Calanques: from 1 June to 30 September access to the massif is regulated for fire risk and can be closed entirely on 'red' days, so check the Prefecture status from around 6 pm the day before

Sugiton requires a free online reservation on set summer dates (in 2026: every day from 27 June to 30 August plus certain weekends in June and September); check the park's booking page for the current year's dates
By public transport: bus 22 to the Les Baumettes stop, then about an hour on foot to Morgiou (per the park's Morgiou page)
Afternoon: Marseille Vieux-Port seafood dinner

days.title: Marseille to Nice
activities: Train from Marseille to Nice, about 2 hr 40 (Nice Côte d'Azur tourist office)
Promenade des Anglais
Evening in Vieux Nice and the Cours Saleya
days.lodging_suggestion: Nice (Vieux Nice or near Nice-Ville station)

days.title: Monaco day trip
activities: TER from Nice to Monaco-Monte-Carlo, about 23 minutes with around sixty round trips a day; TER tickets to Monaco do not need a seat reservation (Monaco tourism site)
Monaco-Monte-Carlo station is underground with several exits
Prince's Palace area and the Oceanographic Museum
Return to Nice by TER
days.drive_time: TER Nice to Monaco, ~23 min each way
days.lodging_suggestion: Nice (Vieux Nice or near Nice-Ville station)

days.title: Nice old town + departure
activities: Climb or ride up Colline du Château for the view over the Baie des Anges
Musée Matisse in the Cimiez district: check opening days before you go
Depart from Nice airport, or take the TGV to Paris (about 6 hours, per the Nice tourist office)
days.drive_time: TGV Nice to Paris, ~6 hr (if not flying)
days.lodging_suggestion: Nice (Vieux Nice or near Nice-Ville station)

food_culture.name: Bouillabaisse
food_culture.description: Marseille's traditional fish stew, closely associated with the Vieux-Port; many harbourside restaurants list it, so ask whether it must be ordered ahead.

food_culture.name: Châteauneuf-du-Pape
food_culture.description: A Rhône wine named for the popes' summer residence near Avignon, and one of the best-known wines of the Avignon area.

food_culture.name: Socca and salade niçoise
food_culture.description: Socca, a chickpea-flour pancake cooked on a large pan, and the raw-vegetable salade niçoise are classic Nice dishes found around Vieux Nice.

food_culture.name: Pastis
food_culture.description: An aniseed spirit diluted with cold water, closely associated with Marseille and Provençal café terraces.

food_culture.name: Provençal markets
food_culture.description: Outdoor markets such as the Cours Saleya market in Nice are part of daily life in Provence and the Riviera, selling produce, flowers and local specialities.

title: Rome, Florence + Venice by Rail, Italy
best_time_description: Spring (April to early June) and early autumn (September to October) are comfortable for walking all three cities and sit outside peak summer; this is an editorial suggestion rather than met-service data. Museum opening days drive the order: the Uffizi is closed on Mondays, and the Vatican Museums are open Monday to Saturday plus the last Sunday of the month (free entry that day).
description: Italy's classic first-timer arc by high-speed train, no car needed: three days in Rome, a fast Italo/Frecciarossa-type hop to Florence for the Renaissance museums, then on to Venice.

days.title: Arrive Rome
activities: Check in and walk the historic centre: Piazza Navona and the Trevi Fountain, both open public squares
Evening meal in a trattoria in the centre
days.lodging_suggestion: Rome (near Termini or the historic centre)

days.title: Colosseum, Roman Forum + Palatine
activities: Colosseum, Roman Forum and Palatine: buy a timed-entry ticket only from the Parco archeologico del Colosseo's official ticketing site (ticketing.colosseo.it); the Colosseum entry is fixed to the booked time and the park advises arriving at the Colosseum entrance 15 minutes before it
The Forum and Palatine can be done before or after the Colosseum slot on the standard ticket
Evening walk back through the centre
days.lodging_suggestion: Rome (near Termini or the historic centre)

days.title: Vatican Museums
activities: Vatican Museums and the Sistine Chapel: book online only at tickets.museivaticani.va, which the museums name as their only official online ticket site (beware look-alike sites). Open Monday to Saturday 8:00-20:00 (last entry 18:00) and the last Sunday of each month 9:00-14:00 (last entry 12:30), when entry is free; check the closure calendar for your dates
St Peter's Basilica is next door; check its own opening and dress rules before you go
Afternoon free in the centre
days.lodging_suggestion: Rome (near Termini or the historic centre)

days.title: Rome to Florence
activities: Italo high-speed train Rome to Florence, about 1 hour 25 minutes (Italo destinations page); Trenitalia also runs frequent Frecciarossa services on the route, which Trenitalia describes as just over 1 hour 30 minutes, so compare times on the day
Walk to Piazza del Duomo and the Ponte Vecchio
Evening in the Oltrarno district across the Arno

days.title: Uffizi + Accademia
activities: Uffizi Gallery: open Tuesday to Sunday 8:15-18:30, closed Mondays, 1 January and 25 December; a ticket bought in advance for a set date is a named ticket (EUR 29 versus EUR 25 on the day, per the Uffizi site), so book on uffizi.it

Galleria dell'Accademia (Michelangelo's David): book entry on the museum's official booking site via galleriaaccademiafirenze.it and check its opening days first; admission is free on the first Sunday of each month, and free days cannot be pre-booked
Late afternoon on the Ponte Vecchio and along the Arno

days.title: Florence to Venice
activities: Italo high-speed train Florence to Venice, about 2 hours (Italo destinations page, which says the time depends on the date and time of day), so check the timetable for your train
Arrive on the Grand Canal and walk to your lodging; Venice has no cars, so expect to walk or use public water transport
Evening cicchetti round of the bacari (small bars) in Cannaregio or San Polo
days.lodging_suggestion: Venice (historic centre, or Mestre if on a budget)

days.title: Venice: San Marco + the lagoon
activities: Piazza San Marco and the Doge's Palace: buy tickets from the official Doge's Palace site (palazzoducale.visitmuve.it, which sells through Vivaticket) and check the opening hours for your date; some tickets there have no entry time slot, so check the ticket type

Venice's day-visitor access fee was charged only on set days in spring and summer 2026 (3 April to 26 July) and the city's portal said it no longer applied from 27 July; check cda.ve.it for the rules on your dates
Wander the canals away from San Marco
days.lodging_suggestion: Venice (historic centre, or Mestre if on a budget)

days.title: Depart Venice
activities: Last morning in the city
Rail onward, or depart from Venice by air (check the airport transfer in advance)
days.lodging_suggestion: Venice (historic centre, or Mestre if on a budget)

food_culture.name: Italian cooking
food_culture.description: UNESCO inscribed 'Italian cooking, between sustainability and biocultural diversity' on its intangible cultural heritage list in 2025.

food_culture.name: Sarde in saor and baccalà mantecato
food_culture.description: Sardines in a sweet-and-sour onion marinade and creamed salt cod are typical Venetian cicchetti (small bites), eaten informally at bacari standing up, according to Venice's official tourism site (Venezia Unica).

food_culture.name: Andar per ombre
food_culture.description: The Venetian custom of going from bacaro to bacaro for a small glass of wine and cicchetti, a social evening ritual rather than a sit-down meal; the districts of Cannaregio and San Polo are named by Italy's tourism site as home to many bacari.

food_culture.name: Opera singing in Italy
food_culture.description: UNESCO listed 'The practice of opera singing in Italy' as intangible heritage in 2023; if you want to attend a performance, check the opera houses' own programmes for your dates.

food_culture.name: Free first Sundays at state museums
food_culture.description: Both the Accademia in Florence and the MANN archaeology museum in Naples state free admission on the first Sunday of each month; free tickets cannot be booked in advance and are collected on the day, so expect queues.

title: Naples, Pompeii, Capri + the Amalfi Coast, Italy
best_time_description: Late spring (May to June) and early autumn (September to early October) suit ferries, coastal walks and Pompeii's open-air site and avoid peak-summer crowds; this is an editorial suggestion rather than met-service data. Ferry and shuttle timetables on the Amalfi Coast and to Capri change by season, so check each operator's timetable for your dates.
description: A south-Italy route without a car: Naples for archaeology and pizza, a Pompeii day by train, a fast ferry to Capri, then Salerno and a ferry to Amalfi, with Positano or the Path of the Gods as day options.

days.title: Arrive Naples
activities: Italo high-speed train from Rome to Naples takes about 1 hour (Italo destinations page); allow more time if arriving from elsewhere
Stroll the historic centre (UNESCO World Heritage, inscribed 1995) around Spaccanapoli
Evening pizza in the old town
days.lodging_suggestion: Naples (historic centre or near Napoli Centrale)

days.title: Naples: archaeology museum + old town
activities: Museo Archeologico Nazionale di Napoli (MANN): closed Tuesdays (except some public holidays) and not every gallery is open every day while rooms are being renovated, so check the 'schedule of open rooms' on museoarcheologiconapoli.it and buy tickets through its official sales channel; admission is free on the first Sunday of the month
Afternoon in the historic centre
days.lodging_suggestion: Naples (historic centre or near Napoli Centrale)

days.title: Pompeii day trip
activities: Circumvesuviana Napoli-Sorrento line to Pompei Scavi-Villa dei Misteri, about 40 minutes (EAV's own timetable valid from 17 October 2026 shows 36 to 39 minutes from Napoli Garibaldi and Porta Nolana); Trenitalia regional trains also serve Pompei station, so check both timetables on the day

Pompeii archaeological park: tickets are personal (named) and sold online through the park's official site, with ticket offices at Porta Marina, Piazza Anfiteatro and Piazza Esedra; hours change with the season (9:00-17:00, last entry 15:30, from 15 October to 15 March; 9:00-19:00, last entry 17:30, from 16 March to 14 October); closed 25 December and 1 January; free on the first Sunday of the month
Return to Naples by train
days.drive_time: Circumvesuviana Naples to Pompei Scavi, ~40 min each way
days.lodging_suggestion: Naples (historic centre or near Napoli Centrale)

days.title: Capri day trip
activities: SNAV fast ferry from Napoli Molo Beverello to Capri, about 50 minutes (SNAV timetable page); other operators and Caremar sail from Naples too, with slower ferries taking longer
Capri town and the Piazzetta, and a walk to the Giardini di Augusto (check opening times)
Check the last sailing back to Naples before you commit to an evening on the island
days.drive_time: SNAV fast ferry Naples to Capri, ~50 min each way
days.lodging_suggestion: Naples (historic centre or near Napoli Centrale)

days.title: Naples to Salerno to Amalfi
activities: Italo high-speed train Naples to Salerno, about 35 minutes (Italo destinations page)

Travelmar ferry Salerno to Amalfi, about 35 minutes on direct sailings (Travelmar's timetable also lists some sailings via Vietri, Cetara, Maiori and Minori that take 60 minutes; check the current timetable)
Amalfi's cathedral square and the lanes behind the harbour

days.title: Positano or the Path of the Gods
activities: Option A: Travelmar ferry from Amalfi to Positano, about 25 minutes each way (Travelmar timetable), and a day on the beach and the stepped lanes

Option B: the Path of the Gods trail: Travelmar's page describes a shuttle from Amalfi to Bomerano (Piazza Capasso), the trailhead, with a morning ferry-plus-shuttle connection from Positano taking about 1 hour 40 minutes in total; Travelmar gives no walking time for the trail itself, so plan the return with the shuttle or ferry timetable
Return to Amalfi by ferry or shuttle
days.drive_time: Travelmar Amalfi to Positano, ~25 min each way

days.title: Amalfi to Salerno + depart
activities: Travelmar ferry Amalfi to Salerno, about 35 minutes on direct sailings (some sailings via other towns take 60 minutes; check the current timetable)
Onward by train from Salerno (Italo Salerno to Naples, about 35 minutes) or depart by rail from Salerno
days.drive_time: Travelmar ferry ~35 min + Italo Salerno to Naples ~35 min

food_culture.name: Art of the Neapolitan pizzaiuolo
food_culture.description: UNESCO inscribed the art of the Neapolitan 'pizzaiuolo' on its intangible cultural heritage list in 2017; it recognises the craft of the pizza-maker (dough, shaping and wood-fired baking) rather than the dish itself.

food_culture.name: Mozzarella di Bufala Campana
food_culture.description: A buffalo-milk cheese with an EU protected designation of origin (first registered in 1996), which may only be made in a defined area covering parts of Campania and neighbouring regions.

food_culture.name: Limone Costa d'Amalfi
food_culture.description: Lemons from the Amalfi Coast carry an EU protected geographical indication, so lemons sold under that name must come from the designated coastal area.

food_culture.name: Mediterranean diet
food_culture.description: UNESCO's intangible cultural heritage list for Italy includes the Mediterranean diet (inscribed 2013).

title: Madrid, Toledo, Seville + Granada, Spain
best_time_description: Spring and autumn are the editorial pick for walking Madrid and the Andalusian cities on foot; this is a suggestion, not met-service data, so check the climate table for your month. Check each museum's weekly closing day before fixing the order of days.
description: A classic first-timer rail loop from the capital: Madrid and a half-hour Avant hop to UNESCO-listed Toledo, high-speed AVE south to Seville, a Renfe Avant on to Granada and the Alhambra, then back to Madrid. All by train, no car.

days.title: Arrive Madrid
activities: Check in and walk the Plaza Mayor area
Evening tapas around the old centre, or a visit to the San Miguel market, a converted traditional market now a gourmet destination

days.title: Prado, Retiro + Royal Palace
activities: Prado Museum, one of the major museums of the world; book on the museum's official site and check its opening hours before you go
Retiro Park and the Paseo del Prado boulevard, together on the UNESCO World Heritage List
Royal Palace; check opening days and any ceremonial closures on the official Patrimonio Nacional site

days.title: Toledo day trip
activities: Renfe Avant from Madrid Puerta de Atocha to Toledo, about 30 minutes (Spain's tourism board); the first train from Atocha leaves at 6:45 am (Renfe), the first Toledo-Madrid Avant at 6:25 am runs Monday to Friday only, and the last Madrid-Toledo train at 8:45 pm runs Sunday to Thursday, so check Renfe's timetable for your day's last return

Toledo's old town is a World Heritage site: the Gothic Cathedral, the Alcazar that dominates the skyline, Santa Maria la Blanca (the oldest synagogue in the city) and the Church of Santo Tome with El Greco's Burial of the Count of Orgaz
Return to Madrid in the evening

days.title: AVE to Seville
activities: AVE from Madrid Puerta de Atocha to Sevilla Santa Justa, from about 2 hours 30 minutes (Spain's tourism board); Renfe's first departure is at 07:00
Afternoon in the old town around the Cathedral, the largest Gothic cathedral in Europe, and its Giralda tower
Evening tapas in Triana

days.title: Alcazar, Plaza de Espana + flamenco
activities: Real Alcazar palace and gardens: buy tickets from the official Real Alcazar site and check its opening hours before you go
Plaza de Espana
Evening flamenco at a tablao or neighbourhood peña; reserve ahead

days.title: Avant to Granada
activities: Renfe Avant from Sevilla Santa Justa to Granada, about 2 hours 37 to 2 hours 45 minutes on the four direct Avant trains in Renfe's online timetable for 18 October 2026 (07:40, 09:55, 12:17 and 19:15 departures; schedules change, so recheck on renfe.com)
Walk the Albaicin, a World Heritage neighbourhood
Evening in the old town; tapas

days.title: The Alhambra
activities: Alhambra and Generalife (World Heritage): buy tickets only through the official ticket site linked from alhambra-patronato.es and book well ahead; tickets are personal and non-transferable, each visitor needs a personal ID document, and entry to the Nasrid Palaces is at a fixed time (300 people every half hour) and you are refused if you miss your slot
Afternoon free in the Albaicin or Sacromonte

days.title: Return to Madrid + depart
activities: Train from Granada to Madrid, from about 3 hours 30 minutes (Spain's tourism board); check the Renfe timetable for the exact service
Depart from Madrid

food_culture.name: Tapas in Triana
food_culture.description: Seville's tourism board recommends Triana, the district known for traditional ceramics and handicrafts, for tapas.

food_culture.name: Flamenco in Seville
food_culture.description: Spain's tourism board notes you can see flamenco at a tablao or a neighbourhood peña in Seville, and that the city hosts the Biennial, a major international flamenco festival.

food_culture.name: San Miguel market, Madrid
food_culture.description: A converted traditional market that Spain's tourism board calls a gastronomic shrine, good for grazing on small plates in the centre.

food_culture.name: Tapas culture
food_culture.description: Ordering several small plates and moving between bars is an ordinary way to eat in Madrid, Seville and Granada rather than a tourist ritual.

title: Barcelona, Valencia + Mallorca, Spain
best_time_description: Late spring and early autumn suit city walking and a Mediterranean island at a comfortable pace and avoid peak summer crowds; this is an editorial suggestion, not met-service data. Ferry frequency varies by season, so check the operator's schedule for your dates.
description: Spain's Mediterranean side: three days in Barcelona, a Euromed train down the coast to Valencia, then a ferry crossing of 7 to 9 hours (Baleària describes its Valencia-Palma sailing as an overnight crossing) to Mallorca and Palma's old town.

days.title: Arrive Barcelona
activities: Check in and walk the old town, then La Boqueria, a traditional market

days.title: Gaudi's Barcelona
activities: Sagrada Familia: tickets are for a chosen time slot and late arrivals are refused entry, so buy ahead only through the official sagradafamilia.org site or app and check its current opening hours (they vary by month and day of the week)
Casa Batllo, one of the famous Gaudi sights; book ahead on its official site
Park Guell: tickets are sold online only for an assigned entry time, with 30 minutes after that time to get in; buy on the official parkguell.barcelona site

days.title: Montjuic + old town
activities: Montjuic park for views over the city and port
Afternoon in the old town
Evening at a neighbourhood tapas bar

days.title: Euromed to Valencia
activities: Renfe Euromed from Barcelona Sants to Valencia, about 2 hours 47 minutes to 3 hours 26 minutes depending on the train (Renfe's online timetable for 18 October 2026 lists Euromed departures at 10:15, 16:15, 18:15 and 20:15; schedules change, so recheck on renfe.com)
Evening in the old centre
days.lodging_suggestion: Valencia (old town or near the Turia gardens)

days.title: Central Market + Silk Exchange
activities: Central Market, a Modernist market that Spain's tourism board calls Europe's largest fresh produce market; check its opening days before going
La Lonja de la Seda (Silk Exchange), a World Heritage building with an orange-tree courtyard
Paella lunch
days.lodging_suggestion: Valencia (old town or near the Turia gardens)

days.title: City of Arts and Sciences + Albufera
activities: City of Arts and Sciences by Santiago Calatrava and Felix Candela, including the Oceanografic, which the tourism board calls Europe's largest aquarium
Sunset at the Albufera, a navigable lake beside the sea
days.lodging_suggestion: Valencia (old town or near the Turia gardens)

days.title: Ferry to Mallorca
activities: Ferry from Valencia to Palma, 7 to 9 hours depending on the vessel (Baleària lists 7 to 9 hours and describes the Valencia-Palma sailing as an overnight crossing that reaches Palma early in the morning, with cabins available). Check the operator's timetable for your date and book in advance
Settle into Palma's old town on arrival

days.title: Palma old town
activities: Palma Cathedral (La Seu), which Spain's tourism board lists as a must-see
Almudaina Palace and the Lonja (the Exchange) nearby
Evening in the old town

days.title: Mallorca by the mountains
activities: Sierra de Tramuntana villages of Soller and Valldemossa, both described by Spain's tourism board; the TIB public bus line 203 (timetable valid from 1 March 2026) links Palma, Valldemossa, Deia and Soller, taking about 30 minutes from Palma to Valldemossa and about 1 hour to 1 hour 5 minutes to Soller; recheck times at tib.org
Return to Palma

days.title: Depart Palma
activities: Depart from Palma de Mallorca; check flight times back to the mainland or home
days.lodging_suggestion: Palma (near the airport or the port)

food_culture.name: Paella in Valencia
food_culture.description: Spain's tourism board calls paella Valencia's star dish and recommends paella by the sea at beaches such as Malvarrosa, with El Palmar known for its paella.

food_culture.name: La Boqueria
food_culture.description: A traditional market in Barcelona that Spain's tourism board names among the city's markets; good for browsing local produce.

food_culture.name: Valencia Central Market
food_culture.description: A Modernist covered market that Spain's tourism board calls Europe's largest fresh produce market; wandering the stalls is a highlight of the city.

food_culture.name: Tapas culture
food_culture.description: Eating several small plates at a bar is an ordinary way to eat in Barcelona and across Spain rather than a tourist ritual.

title: Lisbon, Sintra, Porto + Douro Valley by Train, Portugal
best_time_description: Spring and early autumn suit walking Lisbon and Porto and a day on the Douro line, and avoid the peak-summer crowds at Sintra; this is an editorial suggestion, not met-service data. Jerónimos Monastery and Belém Tower are closed on Mondays, so keep Belém off a Monday.
description: Portugal's classic first-timer line done entirely without a car: three days in Lisbon including Belém and a Sintra day trip, the Alfa Pendular up to Porto, then a day on CP's Linha do Douro to Pinhão in the wine valley.

days.title: Arrive Lisbon
activities: Check in and walk the Baixa and Alfama districts toward the Sé (cathedral) and the miradouros (viewpoints)
Evening dinner in Alfama; fado houses are in this district

days.title: Belém: Jerónimos + Belém Tower
activities: Jerónimos Monastery: the official museusemonumentos.pt site lists it as closed Mondays, 1 January, Easter Sunday, 1 May, 13 June and 25 December; tickets can be bought online there, and the church has shorter hours than the cloister

Belém Tower (Torre de Belém): also closed Mondays on the official site, which lists it open Tuesday to Sunday 9:30 to 17:30; it reopened on 27 May 2026 after restoration and the monument now uses set time slots, so book a ticket online in advance and check the current slot rules
Pastel de nata in Belém and a walk along the Tagus waterfront

days.title: Sintra day trip
activities: CP urban train from Lisboa Rossio to Sintra, about 40 minutes direct on CP's journey planner

Pena Palace: entry to the palace needs a booked time slot bought in advance from the official Parques de Sintra site; if you arrive before your slot you cannot enter, and tickets cannot be changed or refunded if you miss it. The walk from the park entrance to the palace is about 30 minutes
Optional: Monserrate Park and Palace (Parques de Sintra notes roof restoration works with scaffolding until the first quarter of 2027)
Return train to Lisbon in the evening
days.drive_time: CP train Lisboa Rossio to Sintra, ~40 min

days.title: Alfa Pendular to Porto
activities: CP Alfa Pendular from Lisboa Santa Apolónia to Porto Campanhã: CP's timetable valid since 20 September 2026 shows the 09:00 departure (Monday to Saturday) arriving 11:48 (about 2 h 48 min) and the daily 07:00 arriving 09:48; in the opposite direction it shows Porto Campanhã 05:40 to Lisboa Oriente 08:23 (2 h 43 min). Book at cp.pt and check current departures
Walk from São Bento station, whose entrance hall is tiled with azulejos, to the Ribeira waterfront
Dom Luís I Bridge at sunset
days.drive_time: CP Alfa Pendular Lisbon to Porto, ~2 h 45 min

days.title: Porto: Lello + Gaia port lodges
activities: Livraria Lello: buy a timed ticket online from the official Livraria Lello site (tickets are non-refundable and can be moved once, up to 24 hours before); check the day's opening hours on that site
Porto Cathedral (Sé do Porto) and the old streets of the Ribeira
Cross the Dom Luís I Bridge to Vila Nova de Gaia for a port lodge visit and tasting

days.title: Douro Valley by train to Pinhão
activities: CP Linha do Douro InterRegional from Porto Campanhã 09:30 to Régua 11:20 and Pinhão 11:46 (about 2 h 16 min), from CP's timetable valid since 5 August 2026; the 07:30 departure reaches Pinhão at 09:51. Check the timetable on the day, as CP warns that connections are guaranteed only in normal operating conditions
Pinhão station and the terraced vineyards on the river
Lunch in Pinhão and a river or vineyard visit booked locally in advance
Afternoon train back to Porto; the timetable shows departures from Pinhão at 14:07 and 18:11, and the trip back takes about 2 h 20 min, so confirm the arrival time at cp.pt
days.drive_time: CP Linha do Douro Porto Campanhã to Pinhão, ~2 h 15 min

days.title: Return to Lisbon + depart
activities: CP Alfa Pendular from Porto Campanhã back to Lisbon, about 2 h 45 min (see day 4 for the sourced times)
Final evening in Lisbon (Chiado or Bairro Alto) or depart from Lisbon airport
days.drive_time: CP Alfa Pendular Porto to Lisbon, ~2 h 45 min
days.lodging_suggestion: Lisbon (near your departure airport or station)

food_culture.name: Pastel de nata
food_culture.description: The custard tart sold in bakeries across Lisbon; Belém is the neighbourhood most associated with it.

food_culture.name: Fado
food_culture.description: Portugal's urban song tradition, inscribed by UNESCO on its intangible cultural heritage list in 2011; Lisbon's Alfama and Mouraria districts are where visitors usually hear it live.

food_culture.name: Francesinha
food_culture.description: A Porto sandwich of bread, cured meats and cheese covered with a hot sauce; ask locally where the neighbourhood favourites are.

food_culture.name: Port wine
food_culture.description: A fortified wine from the Douro Valley; the lodges in Vila Nova de Gaia, across the river from Porto, offer tours and tastings.

food_culture.name: Azulejos
food_culture.description: Painted ceramic tiles that cover station halls, churches and house fronts across Portugal; São Bento station in Porto is a well-known example.

title: Alentejo + Algarve by Train, Portugal
best_time_description: May, June, September and October are an editorial suggestion: the Alentejo plain is exposed in midsummer and the Algarve coast is busiest then; this is not met-service data. Evening-only and weekday-only trains are noted in the days below.
description: A slower southern route: an Intercidades to Évora in the Alentejo for two nights, back to Lisbon and down to Faro on the Linha do Sul, then CP's Algarve line west to Lagos and its clifftop coast, all by train.

days.title: Arrive Lisbon
activities: Check in and walk the Baixa, Chiado and the Tagus waterfront
Early night: the Évora train leaves early on weekdays

days.title: Train to Évora
activities: CP Intercidades from Lisboa Oriente 07:02 to Évora 08:47 (about 1 h 45), Monday to Friday; on Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays the 09:58 departure reaches Évora at 11:40 (CP timetable valid since 6 September 2026); a daily train leaves at 17:02 and arrives 18:41. Book at cp.pt
Praça do Giraldo and the old town inside the walls
Évora Cathedral (Sé de Évora) and the Roman Temple
days.drive_time: CP Intercidades Lisboa Oriente to Évora, ~1 h 45

days.title: Évora: Chapel of Bones + countryside
activities: Capela dos Ossos in the Igreja de São Francisco: the chapel is lined with human bones; it uses a paid ticket and seasonal opening hours, with the city council and the church listing slightly different hours, so check the church's own site on the day. Open daily per the council listing, which shows closures on 1 January, Easter Sunday, 25 December and the afternoon of 24 December (that page was last updated in July 2023)
Walk the old town lanes at your own pace
Alentejo dinner: ask for regional dishes at a restaurant in the old town

days.title: Évora to Lisbon to Faro
activities: CP Intercidades Évora 09:14 to Lisboa Oriente 10:57 (daily, 1 h 43)
Lunch in Parque das Nações near Lisboa Oriente during the gap

CP Intercidades Lisboa Oriente 14:02 to Faro 17:39 (daily, about 3 h 37), per CP's September 2026 timetable; book a seat at cp.pt in advance. The 08:23 Alfa Pendular reaches Faro at 11:27 and the 17:23 reaches it at 20:23 if you prefer another departure
days.drive_time: CP Évora to Lisbon ~1 h 45, then Lisbon to Faro ~3 h 35
days.lodging_suggestion: Faro (near the station and old town)

days.title: Faro old town + Ria Formosa
activities: Walk the Cidade Velha (old town) inside Faro's walls, entering through the Arco da Vila
Ria Formosa Natural Park: the lagoon and barrier islands lie directly south of Faro; check which boat operators run on the day
Evening seafood dinner in Faro
days.lodging_suggestion: Faro (near the station and old town)

days.title: Train to Lagos
activities: CP Algarve line from Faro 08:36 to Lagos 10:07 (about 1 h 31), per the CP timetable valid since 19 July 2026, when the line became fully electric with direct trains; check the day's timetable
Lagos old town and the waterfront
Praia Dona Ana
days.drive_time: CP Algarve line Faro to Lagos, ~1 h 30

days.title: Ponta da Piedade + beaches
activities: Walk from Lagos to Ponta da Piedade, a headland of sea cliffs and grottoes just south of the town
Boat tours of the grottoes are sold locally; ask about sea conditions on the day
Beach afternoon at Meia Praia or Praia Dona Ana

days.title: Lagos to Faro to Lisbon
activities: CP Algarve line from Lagos 13:22 to Faro 14:53 (about 1 h 31)
CP Alfa Pendular from Faro 16:00 to Lisboa Oriente 19:05 (about 3 h 05, daily); an earlier Alfa Pendular leaves Faro at 07:00 and reaches Lisboa Oriente at 10:05 (CP September 2026 timetable)
Final evening in Lisbon
days.drive_time: CP Lagos to Faro ~1 h 30, then Faro to Lisbon ~3 h
days.lodging_suggestion: Lisbon (near Lisboa Oriente or your departure airport)

food_culture.name: Cataplana
food_culture.description: A seafood stew cooked and served in a hinged copper pan of the same name, a staple of Algarve restaurants.

food_culture.name: Alentejo regional cooking
food_culture.description: The Alentejo is known for hearty bread-based and pork dishes; ask for the day's regional plate at a restaurant in Évora.

food_culture.name: Alentejo wine
food_culture.description: The Alentejo is a major Portuguese wine region; many Évora wine bars pour local reds by the glass.

food_culture.name: Cork oak landscapes
food_culture.description: The Alentejo plain is dotted with cork oaks; Portugal is a leading cork producer, and cork goods are sold in Évora's shops.

food_culture.name: Capela dos Ossos
food_culture.description: Évora's Chapel of Bones, in the Igreja de São Francisco, is a memento mori chapel lined with human bones.

title: Athens, Delphi + Nafplio, Greece
best_time_description: Spring and autumn are comfortable for climbing archaeological sites on foot and sit outside the peak summer crowds; this is an editorial suggestion rather than met-service data. The Epidaurus theatre hosts festival performances in summer, so a summer trip can pair Day 7 with an evening show, but check dates and tickets in advance.
description: A bus-only first-timer's Greece: three days in Athens, an overnight at Delphi on the slopes of Mount Parnassus, then Nafplio in the Peloponnese with a half-day at the ancient theatre of Epidaurus. Every leg is a KTEL intercity bus from Athens, no car needed.

days.title: Arrive Athens
activities: Check in and walk the old streets of Plaka and the Anafiotika quarter below the Acropolis rock
Evening meal in Plaka or Monastiraki

days.title: Acropolis + Acropolis Museum
activities: Acropolis of Athens: entry is by timed slot, so book your slot in advance on the Hellenic Ministry of Culture's official ticketing platform (reported as hhticket.gr; confirm the address and current opening hours there before paying) and go in the first morning slot if you can
Acropolis Museum at the foot of the hill; opening days and ticket prices were not verified, so check its official site
Afternoon in Plaka and Monastiraki

days.title: Ancient Agora + National Archaeological Museum
activities: Ancient Agora of Athens with the Temple of Hephaestus; opening days and entry rules were not verified, so check the Ministry of Culture ticket site
National Archaeological Museum; opening days were not verified, so check its official site
Evening walk or climb up Lycabettus Hill for views over the city

days.title: Athens to Delphi
activities: Intercity KTEL bus from Athens to Delphi: the Greek National Tourism Organisation gives about 2.5 hours; the KTEL Fokidas Athens agency is at Liosion 260 and its regular timetable is on ktel-fokidas.gr (departure times not verified here, so check the day before)

Afternoon at the Delphi archaeological site, the ancient oracle of Apollo on the slopes of Mount Parnassus; opening days and ticket details were not verified, so check the Ministry of Culture ticket site
Evening in the town of Delphi
days.drive_time: KTEL bus Athens to Delphi, about 2.5 hours (Greek National Tourism Organisation)

days.title: Delphi and back to Athens
activities: Morning at the Delphi Archaeological Museum, beside the site; opening days were not verified, so check before you go
KTEL bus back to Athens, the same Athens-Delphi service (allow about 2.5 hours; return timetable on ktel-fokidas.gr)
Evening in Athens
days.drive_time: KTEL bus Delphi to Athens, about 2.5 hours

days.title: Athens to Nafplio
activities: Intercity KTEL bus from Athens to Nafplio: the Greek National Tourism Organisation gives about 1.5 to 2 hours (departure terminal and times not verified, so check with KTEL before you travel)
Walk Nafplio's old town and the seafront
Bourtzi, the fortress on the islet of Agioi Theodoroi just off the waterfront
days.drive_time: KTEL bus Athens to Nafplio, about 1.5 to 2 hours (Greek National Tourism Organisation)

days.title: Palamidi + Epidaurus
activities: Palamidi, the castle on the hill above Nafplio with views over the sea and the old town's red roofs
Bus to Epidaurus, about 1 hour from Nafplio (Greek National Tourism Organisation)

Ancient Theatre of Epidaurus, built around 340 to 330 BC and part of the Sanctuary of Asklepios UNESCO World Heritage Site; opening hours and ticket prices were not verified, so check the Ministry of Culture ticket site, and book ahead for any festival performance
Return to Nafplio by bus
days.drive_time: Bus Nafplio to Epidaurus, about 1 hour each way (Greek National Tourism Organisation)

days.title: Return to Athens + depart
activities: KTEL bus from Nafplio back to Athens, about 1.5 to 2 hours (same service as Day 6)
Allow generous time before an onward flight
days.drive_time: KTEL bus Nafplio to Athens, about 1.5 to 2 hours
days.lodging_suggestion: Athens (near your departure point or airport)

food_culture.name: The Mediterranean diet
food_culture.description: Inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2013, shared between Greece, Cyprus, Croatia, Spain, Italy, Morocco and Portugal; a shared table of olive oil, vegetables, bread and fish is the everyday version you will meet in tavernas.

food_culture.name: Rebetiko
food_culture.description: A music and dance tradition that emerged among urban working-class communities in the early 1900s, inscribed by UNESCO in 2017 for Greece; Athens has venues that play it live, which are worth looking up for an evening.

food_culture.name: The oracle at Delphi
food_culture.description: The ancient oracle of Apollo on the slopes of Mount Parnassus, one of the most renowned oracles of antiquity according to the Greek National Tourism Organisation.

food_culture.name: Epidaurus theatre and festival
food_culture.description: The ancient theatre has hosted performances every summer since the 1950s as part of the Athens Epidaurus Festival, per the Greek National Tourism Organisation.

title: Paros, Naxos + Santorini, Greece
best_time_description: Ferry frequency and fast-boat service on this route are strongly seasonal. Blue Star's own destination pages list daily routes to Paros, Naxos and Santorini, but fast boats (SeaJets) mainly run in summer and we could not confirm an official timetable or end date, so in autumn plan on the slower conventional Blue Star ferries and allow extra time; weather also causes cancellations (Blue Star was publishing weather-related schedule changes on its site in mid-October 2026). Late May to September gives the most choice of sailings; shoulder months are quieter. This is an editorial suggestion, not met-service data.
description: A Cyclades island-hop in the classic order from Athens: ferry from Piraeus to Paros, on to Naxos, then Santorini, and back to Athens. Ferries are the connective tissue here, so every hop below says where its timing comes from and what the seasonal caveat is.

days.title: Arrive Athens
activities: Check in near Piraeus or central Athens so the ferry port is easy to reach next morning
Evening walk in Plaka or around Piraeus harbour

days.title: Ferry Piraeus to Paros
activities: Blue Star Ferries conventional ferry from Piraeus to Paros: Blue Star's own page says the journey lasts 4 hours 10 minutes, with daily routes to and from Paros; departure times differ by day, so check the booking page for the exact sailing and book ahead
Arrive in Parikia and walk the old town and the harbour
Panagia Ekatontapyliani (the Church of a Hundred Doors) in Parikia
days.drive_time: Blue Star ferry Piraeus to Paros, 4 hours 10 minutes (Blue Star Ferries)

days.title: Paros: Naoussa + Lefkes
activities: Naoussa, the fishing harbour town on the north coast
Lefkes, the hill village inland
Local buses and rental cars run between the villages; no bus times were verified, so check on the island

days.title: Ferry Paros to Naxos
activities: Sea hop Paros to Naxos: Blue Star's own pages list a Paros to Naxos connection, and fast boats such as SeaJets also serve it in summer, but we could not confirm a current fast-boat timetable, so check seajets.com. On a conventional Blue Star sailing, the operator's 30 July 2026 notice (a weather-adjusted timetable for that day) shows the ship leaving Paros at 22:15 and reaching Naxos at 23:15, so allow about an hour and expect a late-night arrival; check the booking page for your date
The Portara, the marble gateway of the unfinished temple on the Palatia islet beside Naxos town, at sunset
Naxos Chora and its Venetian-era Kastro
days.drive_time: About 1 hour on the Blue Star conventional sailing (Blue Star notice for 30 July 2026); fast-boat time not confirmed

days.title: Naxos villages
activities: Temple of Demeter near Sangri, in the Naxos countryside
Halki and Apeiranthos, two of the island's mountain villages
Local buses or a rental car are the way around; no bus times were verified, so check in Naxos town

days.title: Ferry Naxos to Santorini
activities: Sea hop Naxos to Santorini: Blue Star's own Naxos page lists Santorini as a destination from Naxos. The operator's 30 July 2026 notice shows the ship leaving Naxos at 23:45 and reaching Santorini at 02:00, about 2 hours 15 minutes and arriving in the small hours. Fast boats (SeaJets) also serve this leg in summer, but we could not confirm a current timetable, so check seajets.com
Settle into Fira on the caldera rim
Walk the caldera edge in Fira
days.drive_time: About 2 hours 15 minutes on the Blue Star conventional sailing (Blue Star notice for 30 July 2026); fast-boat time not confirmed

days.title: Santorini: Akrotiri + Oia
activities: Akrotiri, the Bronze Age town buried by the volcanic eruption: the Ministry of Culture hours page (cyclades.culture.gov.gr) lists Monday and Thursday 08:30-15:30, and other days 08:00-18:00 for 16-31 October (last entry 17:30), with tickets at 20 euros full and 10 euros reduced; hours shorten through autumn and winter hours were not listed on that page, so check it before you go
Oia at the north tip of the island for sunset; it is crowded at the evening, so arrive early
A Santorini winery visit; book ahead, hours not verified

days.title: Return to Athens
activities: Ferry Santorini to Piraeus: Blue Star states the Piraeus to Santorini journey lasts from 6 hours 6 minutes (sailings vary, and a slower sailing takes longer). Sailing days and times were not verified for your date, so check the booking page
Santorini also has an airport with flights to Athens; flight times and airlines were not verified here, so check with the airline
Leave at least a full day of slack before an international flight home, because ferries are weather-dependent
days.drive_time: Blue Star ferry Santorini to Piraeus, from 6 hours 6 minutes (Blue Star Ferries)
days.lodging_suggestion: Athens or Piraeus (near your departure point)

food_culture.name: Fava Santorinis
food_culture.description: Fava Santorinis has EU protected designation of origin status (granted in 2010), made from the seeds of Lathyrus clymenum grown on eight Cyclades islands and milled locally.

food_culture.name: Graviera Naxou
food_culture.description: Graviera Naxou is a cheese with an EU protected-name registration (listed in Commission Regulation (EC) No 1107/96); look for it in Naxos tavernas and food shops.

food_culture.name: The Mediterranean diet
