food_culture.description: Inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2013, shared between Greece, Cyprus, Croatia, Spain, Italy, Morocco and Portugal; on the islands this shows up as vegetables, olive oil, bread and fish.

food_culture.name: Akrotiri
food_culture.description: The Bronze Age settlement on Santorini was buried by a volcanic eruption and is an archaeological site you can visit; the Ministry of Culture ticket site has current access details.

title: London, Bath + Oxford, England
best_time_description: Late spring (May-June) and early autumn (September) are comfortable for walking London and for day trips to Bath and Oxford and sit outside the peak July-August crowds; this is an editorial suggestion rather than met-service data.
description: England's classic first-timer arc: five days of London's landmarks and museums, plus two easy rail day trips from Paddington, to Georgian Bath (about 1 hour 20 minutes) and to Oxford's colleges (about 1 hour). No car needed.

days.title: Arrive London
activities: Arrive and check in; ETA holders and visa holders should have their approval ready before boarding
Evening walk along the South Bank from Westminster Bridge past the London Eye toward Tower Bridge
days.lodging_suggestion: London (South Bank, Bloomsbury or near Paddington)

days.title: Tower of London + the City
activities: Tower of London: check the Historic Royal Palaces website for current opening days and hours and book tickets online ahead; see the Crown Jewels and the White Tower
Walk across Tower Bridge
St Paul's Cathedral and the Millennium Bridge toward Tate Modern
days.lodging_suggestion: London (South Bank, Bloomsbury or near Paddington)

days.title: Westminster + museums
activities: Westminster Abbey and the Houses of Parliament exterior: check the Abbey's opening days before you go
St James's Park to Buckingham Palace
The British Museum, which has free general entry (special exhibitions may be ticketed)
days.lodging_suggestion: London (South Bank, Bloomsbury or near Paddington)

days.title: Day trip to Bath
activities: GWR train from London Paddington to Bath Spa, about 1 hour 20 minutes (GWR's fastest service is 1 hour 19 minutes; trains run roughly every 30 minutes)
Bath Abbey and the Roman Baths: check the Roman Baths website for current opening hours and ticket booking
Royal Crescent and the Circus, then the Pulteney Bridge
Return train to Paddington in the evening
days.lodging_suggestion: London (South Bank, Bloomsbury or near Paddington)
days.drive_time: GWR train, about 1 hr 20 min each way

days.title: Day trip to Oxford
activities: Train from London Paddington to Oxford, about 1 hour (GWR's fastest service is 52 minutes; up to 168 trains a day)
Walk the college quads and the Radcliffe Camera; check each college's visiting days, as colleges close to visitors during term events and exams
The Ashmolean Museum (free entry)
Punting or a riverside walk on the Cherwell or Thames, then return to London
days.lodging_suggestion: London (South Bank, Bloomsbury or near Paddington)
days.drive_time: GWR train, about 1 hr each way

days.title: Markets, galleries + West End
activities: Borough Market or Portobello Road Market for lunch (check market days before going)
National Gallery on Trafalgar Square (free entry)
Evening in the West End theatres; book seats in advance
days.lodging_suggestion: London (South Bank, Bloomsbury or near Paddington)

days.title: Depart London
activities: Morning at leisure: Hyde Park and Kensington Gardens
Travel to the airport for departure
days.lodging_suggestion: London (South Bank, Bloomsbury or near Paddington)

food_culture.name: Afternoon tea
food_culture.description: A tea service of sandwiches, scones with clotted cream and jam, and cakes, served in London hotels and tea rooms and in Bath's tea rooms; booking ahead is usual at the well-known venues.

food_culture.name: Fish and chips
food_culture.description: Battered fish with chips, a standard British takeaway and sit-down dish found in every town on this route.

food_culture.name: Sunday roast
food_culture.description: A weekend lunch of roast meat, roast potatoes, Yorkshire pudding and gravy, served in pubs across London, Bath and Oxford.

food_culture.name: Real ale in a pub
food_culture.description: Cask-conditioned beer served in British pubs.

food_culture.name: Oxford college life
food_culture.description: Oxford's colleges are working academic communities, which is why some quads and chapels are closed to visitors at certain times; check each college's visiting hours.

title: Edinburgh, Scottish Highlands + Isle of Skye, Scotland
best_time_description: Late spring to early autumn (May to September) has the longest daylight and the fullest ferry, bus and rail timetables in the Highlands; this is an editorial suggestion rather than met-service data. Some Skye and Highland services run reduced timetables outside summer, so check each operator before booking.
description: A public-transport route north from Scotland's capital: two days in Edinburgh, the train to Inverness, a bus to Skye, then the ferry from Armadale to Mallaig and the West Highland Line south to Fort William and Glasgow.

days.title: Arrive Edinburgh
activities: Arrive and check in; ETA holders and visa holders should have their approval ready before boarding
Walk the Royal Mile from Edinburgh Castle esplanade down toward Holyrood
Evening in the Old Town or Grassmarket

days.title: Edinburgh Castle + Arthur's Seat
activities: Edinburgh Castle, open daily from 9.30am; the official site recommends booking online ahead because tickets often sell out in summer
Holyrood Palace and Holyrood Park
Walk up Arthur's Seat, the hill inside Holyrood Park (wear proper shoes and check the weather)

days.title: Train to Inverness
activities: ScotRail direct train from Edinburgh Waverley to Inverness, about 3 hours 45 minutes on ScotRail's own average figure (fastest services are quicker)
Walk the River Ness and Inverness Castle area
Evening in the city centre

days.title: Inverness to Skye
activities: Citylink bus from Inverness to Portree on Skye, about 3 to 3.5 hours depending on the service; only a few departures run each day, so check the Citylink timetable and book ahead
Check in and walk around Portree harbour

days.title: Skye sights
activities: Without a car, a guided small-group tour from Portree or local buses are the realistic ways to reach the Old Man of Storr, the Quiraing and Fairy Pools; check operators and book ahead
Dunvegan Castle on the west coast
Evening in Portree

days.title: Skye to Mallaig + Fort William
activities: Travel south on Skye to Armadale for the CalMac ferry to Mallaig; the crossing takes about 45 minutes per CalMac, with a limited number of sailings, so check the CalMac timetable and book

Train from Mallaig along the West Highland Line to Fort William (Glasgow Queen Street to Mallaig is about 5 hours 20 minutes in total on ScotRail's figures; check the timetable, as only a few trains run a day)
Evening in Fort William beneath Ben Nevis
days.drive_time: CalMac ferry, about 45 min; then West Highland Line train

days.title: Glenfinnan + train to Glasgow
activities: Visit the Glenfinnan Viaduct viewpoint, reachable by West Highland Line train from Fort William; check the timetable
ScotRail West Highland Line train from Fort William to Glasgow Queen Street, about 4 hours on ScotRail's average figure
Arrive Glasgow for the evening, with onward travel or a flight home next day

food_culture.name: Haggis, neeps and tatties
food_culture.description: Scotland's national dish of spiced offal pudding served with mashed swede and potato, on menus across Edinburgh and the Highlands.

food_culture.name: Cullen skink
food_culture.description: A thick Scottish smoked haddock, potato and onion soup, common in Highland pubs and cafes.

food_culture.name: Scottish seafood
food_culture.description: Langoustines, scallops and mussels landed on the west coast; Skye and Mallaig restaurants and harbour stalls serve local shellfish.

food_culture.name: Scotch whisky
food_culture.description: Scotland's whisky regions include Speyside and the Highlands; Skye has its own distillery, Talisker, at Carbost, which offers distillery visits (check the distillery's own site for how to book).

food_culture.name: Hogmanay and ceilidh
food_culture.description: Scotland's New Year celebration is centred on Edinburgh, and ceilidh dances with live Scottish folk music are held in village halls and pubs across the Highlands and islands.

title: Vancouver, Whistler + Banff to Jasper, Canada
best_time_description: Summer into early autumn suits this route because the Icefields Parkway has services only from early May to mid-October (none between Lake Louise and Jasper in winter), and the Parks Canada Moraine Lake shuttle runs only from June to mid-October. Month choice is an editorial suggestion, not met-service data. From 1 November to 31 March snow tires or chains are legally required on the Icefields Parkway (and winter tires on Highway 99 to Whistler from 1 October), so a winter trip needs the right vehicle and a flexible schedule.
description: Coast to Rockies in nine days: Vancouver and a night in Whistler on the Sea to Sky Highway, a flight to Calgary, then Banff, Lake Louise and Moraine Lake and the 232 km Icefields Parkway to Jasper. A car is needed from Calgary onward. A national parks pass is required in Banff and Jasper.

days.title: Arrive Vancouver
activities: Check in and walk the Stanley Park seawall or Granville Island to ease into the time zone
Evening in Gastown

days.title: Vancouver
activities: Stanley Park: walk or cycle the seawall
Granville Island public market and waterfront
Wander Gastown and Coal Harbour

days.title: Sea to Sky Highway to Whistler
activities: Drive Highway 99 north from Vancouver to Whistler; Destination Vancouver says the drive takes about two hours not counting scenic stops, and Highway 99 is the only road into Whistler. Winter tires are required on the Sea to Sky Highway from 1 October to 31 March (Tourism Whistler)
Stop at Shannon Falls, a roughly 10-minute walk from a parking area just off the highway (Destination Vancouver)
Walk Whistler Village, which is pedestrian-only (Tourism Whistler)
days.drive_time: Vancouver to Whistler ~2 hr by road (Destination Vancouver)

days.title: Whistler back to Vancouver, fly to Calgary
activities: Drive Highway 99 south to Vancouver (about two hours) and return the car at Vancouver airport
Fly Vancouver to Calgary; check airline schedules for current flight times and book a rental car from Calgary airport for the Rockies
days.drive_time: Whistler to Vancouver ~2 hr by road

days.title: Calgary to Banff
activities: Drive west to Banff: the Town of Banff says it is 128 km west of Calgary and the highway trip takes about 1.5 hours, depending on departure point and stops in Canmore
A valid national parks pass is required in Banff National Park (Parks Canada); buy it before you enter the park gates
Walk Banff Avenue and the Bow River; parking in town fills early, so Roam transit or walking is easier
days.drive_time: Calgary to Banff ~1.5 hr (Town of Banff)

days.title: Lake Louise + Moraine Lake
activities: Moraine Lake Road is closed to personal vehicles year-round (Parks Canada). Reserve the Parks Canada shuttle in advance at reservation.pc.gc.ca; for the 2026 season the Lake Louise Lakeshore shuttle ran 15 May to 12 October and the Moraine Lake shuttle 1 June to 12 October, weather permitting, so check the dates for your year
Park free at the Lake Louise Park and Ride if you hold a shuttle reservation; Parks Canada does not recommend driving to the Lakeshore lot, which fills and turns vehicles away
Lake Louise lakeshore walk

days.title: Icefields Parkway to Jasper
activities: Highway 93N, the Icefields Parkway, is 232 km from Lake Louise to Jasper (Parks Canada); allow a full day with stops and start with a full tank, because the only fuel on the route is at Saskatchewan River Crossing and only in summer
Peyto Lake viewpoint, 43 km from Lake Louise (a short walk to the platform); Bow Lake, 39 km north of Lake Louise (Parks Canada)
Columbia Icefield Discovery and Information Centre, 128 km from Lake Louise (visitor centre open May to September)
Athabasca Falls, 31 km from Jasper
Services run early May to mid-October only; in winter there are no services between Lake Louise and Jasper. A national parks pass is required to drive the parkway. Check 511 Alberta before departing
days.drive_time: Banff to Lake Louise, then 232 km to Jasper; a full day with stops (Parks Canada gives distances, not a drive time)

days.title: Jasper: Maligne Lake
activities: Maligne Lake: Parks Canada lists the Maligne Road and Maligne Lake area as reopened after the 2024 wildfire; check the Parks Canada Jasper 'What's open' page for current status
Maligne Canyon and Cavell Road (Cavell Meadows) are listed by Parks Canada as closed for the 2026 season while rehabilitation continues, so do not plan around them without checking
Walk the town of Jasper

days.title: Return south and depart from Calgary
activities: Drive the Icefields Parkway back to Lake Louise and Banff (232 km Lake Louise to Jasper, same stop and services notes as Day 7)
Continue to Calgary airport (Banff to Calgary about 1.5 hr); give yourself a night in Calgary or Banff if you have a morning flight
days.drive_time: Jasper to Lake Louise 232 km; Banff to Calgary ~1.5 hr (Town of Banff)

food_culture.name: Nanaimo bar
food_culture.description: A no-bake layered chocolate, custard and coconut-crumb bar named for Nanaimo on Vancouver Island and found in many British Columbia cafes and bakeries.

food_culture.name: Squamish Lil'wat Cultural Centre, Whistler
food_culture.description: A cultural centre in Whistler run by the Squamish and Lil'wat Nations, whose traditional territories include the Whistler area; check its current opening days and programs before you go.

food_culture.name: Shuttle-and-pass national park etiquette
food_culture.description: Banff, Lake Louise and Jasper are Parks Canada national parks: carry your park pass, reserve the Moraine Lake shuttle, keep your distance from wildlife and pack out all food waste.

title: Toronto, Niagara, Montréal + Québec City, Canada
best_time_description: Late spring to autumn is easiest for walking Old Montréal and Old Québec and for Niagara's outdoor viewpoints; this is an editorial suggestion, not met-service data. Winter works for the cities too but is cold and the Québec City summer-only events (such as the Citadelle's morning music show) do not run.
description: A car-free eastern Canada loop: two days in Toronto, a Niagara Falls day trip by GO train or VIA, then VIA Rail Corridor trains to Montréal and on to Québec City. VIA lists the Toronto to Montréal trip at an average 5 h 13 min and Montréal to Québec City at 3 h 26 min.

days.title: Arrive Toronto
activities: Check in downtown near Union Station, which is the hub for GO and VIA trains
Evening walk on the waterfront or in the Distillery District

days.title: Toronto
activities: CN Tower and the downtown waterfront
St. Lawrence Market South Market: the market's own site lists Tuesday to Friday 9am to 7pm, Saturday 7am to 5pm, Sunday 10am to 5pm and Monday closed, so check current hours before you go
Kensington Market and Chinatown on foot

days.title: Niagara Falls day trip
activities: Train from Toronto: GO Transit says it has service to Niagara Falls all year round (check the timetable for the day you travel; the pages checked do not give a journey time); VIA Rail's route page lists 132 km at an average of 2 h 40 min from Toronto on 2 departures a week, and 1 h 58 min from Niagara Falls back to Toronto on 7 departures a week
Journey Behind the Falls (Niagara Parks): listed as open daily and year-round; Niagara Parks recommends arriving at least an hour before closing
Walk the Niagara Parkway viewpoints, then return to Toronto in the evening
days.drive_time: Toronto to Niagara Falls: VIA ~2 hr 40 min average (132 km), few departures; GO timetable varies

days.title: VIA Rail to Montréal
activities: VIA Rail Corridor train Toronto to Montréal: VIA's route page lists an average of 5 h 13 min over 538 km, with 40 departures a week; book a specific departure on viarail.ca
Evening in Old Montréal (Vieux-Montréal)
days.drive_time: Toronto to Montréal by VIA Rail ~5 hr 13 min average (538 km)

days.title: Montréal
activities: Notre-Dame Basilica: the self-guided sightseeing visit is ticketed through the Basilica's partner Fever, and the Basilica advises buying tickets in advance
Mount Royal on foot
Old Port and Vieux-Montréal streets

days.title: VIA Rail to Québec City
activities: VIA Rail train Montréal to Québec City: VIA's route page lists an average of 3 h 26 min over 270 km, with 34 departures a week
Afternoon in Old Québec: Dufferin Terrace and the Château Frontenac exterior; walk Petit Champlain
days.drive_time: Montréal to Québec City by VIA Rail ~3 hr 26 min average (270 km)

days.title: Québec City
activities: La Citadelle de Québec is open to visitors only with a guide: general admission includes a 60-minute outdoor guided tour in French or English, plus the Royal 22e Régiment Museum

In summer the Citadelle's 10am Changing of the Guard and Music in Red show runs on set days (the Citadelle's 2026 calendar was Wednesday to Sunday, 24 June to 30 August, with exceptions): check its own site for your dates
Walk the ramparts of the old city

days.title: Depart Québec City
activities: Depart from Québec City; to head back to Montréal or Toronto use VIA Rail (Québec City to Montréal about 3 h 19 min on average) and check onward flight times
days.drive_time: Québec City to Montréal by VIA Rail ~3 hr 19 min average

food_culture.name: Poutine
food_culture.description: French fries topped with cheese curds and hot gravy, a Québec dish now served across Canada; try it in Montréal or Québec City.

food_culture.name: Montréal-style bagels
food_culture.description: Hand-rolled, boiled and baked in wood-fired ovens, Montréal bagels are a local specialty distinct from the New York style.

food_culture.name: Niagara icewine
food_culture.description: The Niagara region of Ontario is known for icewine, a sweet wine made from grapes frozen on the vine; look for it at wineries and shops in the region.

food_culture.name: Historic District of Old Québec
food_culture.description: Old Québec was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1985; the old city's ramparts and Lower Town can be explored on foot.

title: Sydney, Melbourne + the Great Ocean Road, Australia
best_time_description: Editorial suggestion, not met-service data: the shoulder seasons (autumn, March to May, and spring, October and November) avoid the summer peak for walking the Blue Mountains and driving the coast road, but check fire danger and total fire bans before any bush or coastal drive (NSW National Parks and the Visit Great Ocean Road site both point to live alerts). Queen Victoria Market trades on Tuesday and Thursday to Sunday only, so order the Melbourne days around that.
description: Australia's classic first-timer arc: Sydney harbour and a Blue Mountains day by train, a 1 hr 35 flight to Melbourne, then a two-night self-drive along the Great Ocean Road to the Twelve Apostles and back.

days.title: Arrive Sydney
activities: Check in and walk Circular Quay and The Rocks
Evening by the harbour with the Opera House in view
days.lodging_suggestion: Sydney (near Circular Quay or Central station)

days.title: Sydney Opera House + the coast
activities: Sydney Opera House: the main guided tour runs about 1 hour and is booked on the official sydneyoperahouse.com site; tours do not run on 25 and 31 December 2026, and the main tour involves roughly 300 stairs with no lift
Royal Botanic Garden Sydney, along the harbour edge
Afternoon: the Bondi to Coogee coastal walk
days.lodging_suggestion: Sydney (near Circular Quay or Central station)

days.title: Blue Mountains day trip
activities: Train from Sydney Central to Katoomba: Visit NSW says express trains take around 90 minutes and all-stops trains up to two hours; you need an Opal card or a contactless bank card to travel
Echo Point lookout (Three Sisters) in Blue Mountains National Park; public buses run from Katoomba to Echo Point
Check NSW National Parks alerts before you go: areas can close for maintenance, weather or fire danger, and total fire bans apply in fire weather
Return to Sydney by train
days.drive_time: Train Sydney Central to Katoomba, ~90 min express / up to 2 hr all stops
days.lodging_suggestion: Sydney (near Circular Quay or Central station)

days.title: Fly to Melbourne
activities: Direct flight Sydney to Melbourne: Virgin Australia gives an average of 1 hr 35 min (Melbourne to Sydney 1 hr 25 min)
Afternoon walk through Melbourne's city-centre laneways and Federation Square
Evening on the Yarra riverfront

days.title: Melbourne: market + city
activities: Queen Victoria Market: its opening-hours page lists trading on Tuesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday (6am to 3pm Tue/Thu/Fri, 6am to 4pm Sat, 9am to 4pm Sun), so swap this day if you arrive on a Monday or Wednesday
Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria and the Shrine of Remembrance area
Late afternoon: collect a hire car for the coast drive on days 6 to 8 (book ahead)

days.title: Melbourne to Torquay + Apollo Bay
activities: Leave Melbourne early: Visit Great Ocean Road lists Torquay, the start of the Great Ocean Road, as 1 hr 17 min from Melbourne CBD
The Great Ocean Road runs 243 km from Torquay to Allansford near Warrnambool

Drive the coast through Lorne to Apollo Bay; the same site quotes about 4 hours (275 km) from Melbourne to the Twelve Apostles by the coast road, so overnighting at Apollo Bay splits that drive; allow a full day with stops
Check VicEmergency and VicTraffic the morning you travel, as the official site advises
days.drive_time: Melbourne to Torquay ~1 hr 17; full Melbourne to Twelve Apostles coast drive ~4 hr (275 km)

days.title: Twelve Apostles + Port Campbell
activities: Twelve Apostles and the Keerray Woorroong Visitor Centre: Visit Great Ocean Road states that from 16 October 2026 every visitor needs to reserve their spot in advance; book through twelveapostles.org.au (check that site for ticket prices). The visitor centre lists daily opening 8am to 8pm and suggests allowing 1 to 2 hours
Continue along the coast to Port Campbell for the night
days.drive_time: Apollo Bay to the Twelve Apostles: no official time found; the full Melbourne to Twelve Apostles run is ~4 hr

days.title: Return to Melbourne
activities: Drive back to Melbourne: Visit Great Ocean Road quotes 275 km and about 4 hours between Melbourne and the Twelve Apostles by the coast road; a same-day out-and-back from Melbourne is possible but the site does not recommend it
Return the hire car and have a last evening in Melbourne
days.drive_time: Twelve Apostles to Melbourne, ~4 hr (275 km, per Visit Great Ocean Road)

days.title: Optional: depart Melbourne
activities: Depart from Melbourne, or fly back to Sydney (about 1 hr 25 min per Virgin Australia) for an international connection

food_culture.name: Flat white and long black coffee
food_culture.description: Café coffee is a daily habit in Melbourne and Sydney; a flat white (espresso with steamed milk) and a long black (espresso over hot water) are standard orders in any city café.

food_culture.name: Meat pie
food_culture.description: A hand-held pastry pie with a meat filling, sold in bakeries, pubs and at sports grounds across Australia and an easy cheap lunch between stops.

food_culture.name: Queen Victoria Market
food_culture.description: Melbourne's central market sells produce, deli goods and specialty food; it trades only on certain days (Tuesday and Thursday to Sunday per its opening-hours page).

food_culture.name: Acknowledgement of Country
food_culture.description: A spoken or written recognition of the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples as the traditional custodians of the land, commonly made at public events, tours and visitor centres you will pass through; the Twelve Apostles precinct is described by Visit Victoria as a sacred landscape.

food_culture.name: Laneway café culture
food_culture.description: Melbourne's CBD laneways hold small cafés and bars, and wandering them is a standard way to spend an afternoon in the city centre.

title: Red Centre Way: Alice Springs, Kings Canyon + Uluru, Australia
best_time_description: Tourism NT says the best time to visit Uluru is May to September, with daytime temperatures of 20 to 30 degrees C; from October to March it can exceed 35 degrees C in the middle of the day. Parks Australia lists late May to July as the cold season with frosty mornings, and late October to December as the hottest. Walk closures apply in heat (see Day 4 and Day 7), so a summer trip needs very early starts.
description: A one-way outback drive along the Red Centre Way from Alice Springs through the West MacDonnell Ranges and Kings Canyon to Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park, ending with a flight out of Ayers Rock airport.

days.title: Arrive Alice Springs
activities: Fly into Alice Springs (Tourism NT describes it as only a few hours' flying time from Australian capital cities) and pick up a hire car; Parks Australia notes cars can be hired at Alice Springs, Yulara or Ayers Rock airport, and that cars at Yulara are limited, so confirm any one-way drop-off terms with the hire company before booking
Visit Alice Springs' Aboriginal art galleries, which Tourism NT highlights

days.title: West MacDonnell Ranges to Glen Helen
activities: Tourism NT's suggested Red Centre Way itinerary lists Alice Springs to Glen Helen as 132 km, on sealed road along Namatjira Drive (Tourism Central Australia)
Simpsons Gap, one of the most prominent gaps in the West MacDonnell Ranges
Ellery Creek Big Hole, a popular picnic, walking and swimming spot in Tjoritja / West MacDonnell National Park (Tourism NT also names Ormiston Gorge and Glen Helen for swimming)
Tourism Central Australia's Mereenie Loop page lists Glen Helen Reception as 'currently unavailable due to closure', so confirm Glen Helen accommodation and fuel are operating before you book
days.drive_time: Alice Springs to Glen Helen, 132 km (Tourism NT; no time stated)

days.title: Glen Helen to Kings Canyon
activities: Tourism NT lists Glen Helen to Kings Canyon as 234 km, and the route uses the Mereenie Loop, an unsealed road Tourism NT recommends only for 4WD vehicles; Tourism Central Australia adds that it is often corrugated with no facilities or fuel stops

A Mereenie Loop permit is required (Tourism NT: pick one up at the Hermannsburg general store; Tourism Central Australia lists the Alice Springs Visitor Information Centre and others, about $5 per vehicle, valid three days), and you must check that your hire car is permitted on unsealed roads and covered by insurance

Without a suitable 4WD, return to Alice Springs and take the fully sealed route to Kings Canyon (Tourism Central Australia: about 5 hours without stops; the Tourism NT Watarrka page says approx. 4 hours)
Optional stop at Tnorala (Gosse Bluff) Conservation Reserve, listed by Tourism NT as a Red Centre Way highlight
Settle in at Kings Canyon / Watarrka National Park and watch the canyon colours change at sunset
days.drive_time: Glen Helen to Kings Canyon, 234 km on the unsealed Mereenie Loop (Tourism NT; no time stated, varies with road condition)

days.title: Kings Canyon Rim Walk + drive to Uluru
activities: Kings Canyon Rim Walk: Tourism NT says allow about 3 to 4 hours; on days forecast to reach 36 degrees C or higher walkers must begin before 9am, and entry is not permitted after that time. Otherwise aim to finish before 10am to avoid the heat
Drive Kings Canyon to Uluru, 300 km per Tourism NT's Red Centre Way itinerary; Tourism NT says Watarrka is about 3 hours' drive from Uluru
Check in at Yulara (Ayers Rock Resort); buy your Uluru-Kata Tjuta park pass online before entering the park
days.drive_time: Kings Canyon to Uluru, 300 km, about 3 hrs (Tourism NT)

days.title: Uluru: Mala walk + sunset
activities: A park pass is required for Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park: Parks Australia lists adults (18+) at $38 for 3 days or $50 annual, children under 18 free; it covers this park only, and it can be bought online or at the entry station
Cultural Centre, open daily from 7.00am; Parks Australia pages give the closing time as 5.45pm or 6.00pm, so check on the day
Mala walk from the Mala carpark to Kantju Gorge: 2 km return, about 1 hr 30, Grade 2
Sunset from the Uluru car sunset viewing area; the park is open every day, with closing times that change by month (Parks Australia publishes the table), and you must leave by closing time
Ayers Rock Resort to Uluru is about 20 minutes' drive (Parks Australia)
days.drive_time: Ayers Rock Resort to Uluru, ~20 min

days.title: Uluru base walk
activities: Uluru base walk: about 10 km around the whole rock, Grade 3; Parks Australia recommends starting clockwise from the Mala carpark in the early morning and, in hot weather, finishing before 11.00am, as some tracks close in summer afternoons
Do not climb Uluru: the climb closed permanently on 26 October 2019 and Parks Australia states penalties apply
Carry at least one litre of water per person per hour (Parks Australia's heat-safety advice); in summer it strongly recommends not walking after 11.00am

days.title: Kata Tjuta
activities: Sunrise at Talinguru Nyakunytjaku (30 minutes from Ayers Rock Resort) or the Kata Tjuta dune viewing area

Valley of the Winds walk: Grade 4, full circuit 3 to 4 hours; Parks Australia states it closes at the first lookout (Karu) from 11am when the forecast or actual temperature reaches 36 degrees C or above. Please do not photograph or film Kata Tjuta's rock formations on this walk, as Anangu ask
Shorter option: Walpa Gorge walk (2.6 km per Tourism NT), with seating inside the gorge
Resort to Kata Tjuta is about 45 minutes' drive (Parks Australia); the 3-day pass bought on Day 5 covers this day
days.drive_time: Ayers Rock Resort to Kata Tjuta, ~45 min

days.title: Fly out of Ayers Rock
activities: Ayers Rock airport (AYQ) is about 10 minutes from the resort; Parks Australia gives approximate flight times of Sydney 3 hr, Melbourne 2 hr 40, Cairns 2 hr 50 and Brisbane 3 hr 15, with Virgin Australia, Qantas and Jetstar named as airlines
Return any one-way hire car at the airport if arranged with the hire company
days.drive_time: Ayers Rock Resort to the airport, ~10 min

food_culture.name: Tjukurpa
food_culture.description: Anangu creation law and culture; Parks Australia presents Uluru and Kata Tjuta as places where many creation stories converge, and the walks are part of learning those stories.

food_culture.name: Bush foods and quandong
food_culture.description: Parks Australia describes Anangu bush foods and tools as part of the park's living culture, with quandongs among the foods shown; seasonal food plants flower and fruit through the year.

food_culture.name: Central Australian Aboriginal art
food_culture.description: Alice Springs' galleries show work by prominent and emerging Indigenous artists (Tourism NT); some remote communities have art centres, and Central Land Council permits are needed to enter most remote Aboriginal communities.

food_culture.name: Outback roadhouses
food_culture.description: Roadhouses along the Stuart and Lasseter Highways offer fuel, hot meals, refreshments and accommodation (Parks Australia); Curtin Springs is the nearest to Yulara, about 100 km away.

food_culture.name: Sounds of Silence dinner
food_culture.description: An outdoor dinner under the desert sky with stargazing at Uluru, listed by Tourism NT as a four-hour experience; book ahead in peak season, May to September.

title: Cape Town, Winelands + Garden Route, South Africa
best_time_description: Editorial suggestion: spring (September to November) combines the southern right whale season on the Cape coast (June to November, per Cape Town Tourism) with open-air days in the Winelands and on the Garden Route; February and March suit the same route without whales. The Table Mountain cableway runs weather permitting and may close in bad weather, so keep that day flexible. Check the Robben Island ferry and the cableway the same morning, as both can be cancelled for weather.
description: A nine-day self-drive from Cape Town through the Franschhoek and Robertson wine valleys, inland along Route 62 to Oudtshoorn and the Cango Caves, then down to Plettenberg Bay, Tsitsikamma and George.

days.title: Arrive Cape Town
activities: Collect your bags at Cape Town International Airport and transfer to the city; Cape Town Tourism places the airport about 20 km from the city centre, and the MyCiTi A01 bus runs from the station outside the main terminal to the Civic Centre in the centre
Evening walk at the V&A Waterfront
days.drive_time: Airport to city centre, about 20 km (Cape Town Tourism)
days.lodging_suggestion: Cape Town (City Bowl or V&A Waterfront)

days.title: Robben Island + Table Mountain
activities: Morning: Robben Island Museum tour. The ferry leaves from the Nelson Mandela Gateway at the V&A Waterfront; the tour takes about 3.5 hours including the ferry, passengers must arrive at least 30 minutes before departure, the museum says early booking is recommended, and it may cancel or retime sailings for weather. Book through the Robben Island Museum site.

Afternoon: Table Mountain Aerial Cableway. It runs weather permitting and may close in bad weather; check the live status on tablemountain.net or the official app before going up. Tickets can be bought online (Webtickets); standard tickets are valid for 7 days and Fast Track tickets book a specific timeslot.
If either is closed by weather, swap the order or move it to the next free morning
days.lodging_suggestion: Cape Town (City Bowl or V&A Waterfront)

days.title: Cape Peninsula: Cape Point + Boulders penguins
activities: Cape of Good Hope section of Table Mountain National Park, run by SANParks: Cape Point lighthouse (on foot or by the Flying Dutchman funicular), Buffelsfontein Visitor Centre, and Eland, Red Hartebeest, Bontebok and Zebra inside the fenced section. Gate tickets are bought through SANParks; swimming at Diaz Beach is not allowed because of rip currents.
Boulders Penguin Colony, Simon's Town: African penguins viewed from boardwalks (a daily conservation fee is payable and parking is limited in peak summer, per SANParks)
Whale season (southern right whales, June to November per Cape Town Tourism): Cape Point and Boyes Drive between St James and Kalk Bay are named as higher vantage points on the False Bay coast
days.lodging_suggestion: Cape Town (City Bowl or V&A Waterfront)

days.title: Cape Town to Franschhoek
activities: Drive to Franschhoek; check a live map on the day for the time, as traffic out of Cape Town varies
Wine tastings in the Franschhoek valley; book each estate's tasting in advance and arrange a designated driver or a driver-guide
Dinner in Franschhoek village
days.drive_time: Cape Town to Franschhoek: check a live map for current traffic

days.title: Franschhoek to Robertson
activities: Drive to Robertson; check a live map for the time and route
Robertson wine valley tastings in the afternoon
Early night: tomorrow is the longest drive of the trip
days.drive_time: Franschhoek to Robertson: check a live map

days.title: Route 62 to Oudtshoorn
activities: Drive Route 62 east from Robertson to Oudtshoorn; South African Tourism describes Cape Town to Oudtshoorn on the R62 as about a 5-hour drive, so allow a long day. Montagu, Barrydale and Calitzdorp lie on this road, so budget time for coffee and fuel stops
Afternoon in the Klein Karoo: an ostrich-farm tour near Oudtshoorn (book with the farm; opening times vary)
days.drive_time: Robertson to Oudtshoorn via Route 62: check a live map; the longest drive of the trip

days.title: Cango Caves + on to Plettenberg Bay
activities: Cango Caves, open 09:00 to 16:00 per the caves' own site; online booking is through the Oudtshoorn municipality booking site. Go early.
Drive south to the coast to Plettenberg Bay by the most direct road, with Knysna on the way; check a live map for the time
Evening on the beach at Plettenberg Bay
days.drive_time: Oudtshoorn to Plettenberg Bay: check a live map

days.title: Tsitsikamma
activities: Drive east to the Tsitsikamma Section of Garden Route National Park; the park is 68 km from Plettenberg Bay per SANParks, so check a live map for the time
Coastal walks in the park (SANParks lists hikes, walks and trails; a daily conservation fee applies and every visitor must hand in the Gate Registration & Indemnity Form with their passport)
Return to Plettenberg Bay for the night
days.drive_time: Plettenberg Bay to Tsitsikamma, 68 km each way (SANParks)

days.title: Knysna + depart from George
activities: Plettenberg Bay to Knysna: Knysna Lagoon waterfront and a late lunch (oysters are a Knysna speciality)
Drive to George Airport, about 70 km from Knysna per one SANParks page (another SANParks page says 60 km), where rental facilities are available per SANParks; fly onward from there
days.drive_time: Plettenberg Bay to Knysna: check a live map; Knysna to George ~70 km (SANParks)

food_culture.name: Cape Malay bobotie
food_culture.description: A spiced, baked minced-meat dish with an egg topping, central to Cape Malay cooking and easy to find in Cape Town, especially around the Bo-Kaap.

food_culture.name: Western Cape wine
food_culture.description: Franschhoek and Robertson, both on this route, are wine valleys of the Western Cape; Pinotage, South Africa's own cross, is the local red to ask about.

food_culture.name: Ostrich
food_culture.description: Oudtshoorn is the centre of South Africa's ostrich farming and ostrich meat appears on menus there.

food_culture.name: Knysna oysters
food_culture.description: Knysna Lagoon is known for oysters, served in restaurants around the Knysna waterfront.

food_culture.name: The braai
food_culture.description: The South African barbecue is a social ritual rather than just a meal; expect a braai if you are invited to someone's home or stay in self-catering accommodation with a grill.

title: Johannesburg + Kruger National Park, South Africa
best_time_description: SANParks says the dry season (April to September) is traditionally the best game viewing in Kruger because vegetation thins and water is limited to rivers and waterholes, with warm dry days and cold nights; the rainy season (October to March) is hot with lush foliage that makes animals harder to see. Kruger is in a malaria-endemic area: ask a travel doctor about prevention before you go. SANParks accommodation is booked in advance through sanparks.org.
description: Two days of Johannesburg history (Apartheid Museum, Constitution Hill, Soweto), a one-hour Airlink flight to Skukuza, and three nights self-driving Kruger from SANParks camps at Skukuza and Lower Sabie.

days.title: Arrive Johannesburg
activities: Arrive at OR Tambo International Airport and transfer to your hotel
Complete the SARS online traveller declaration before you travel (mandatory for all travellers since 1 July 2026)
Rest day: the Kruger days start early

days.title: Apartheid Museum + Constitution Hill
activities: Apartheid Museum: open Tuesday to Sunday 09:00 to 17:00 and most public holidays (so closed Mondays); book tickets online

Constitution Hill, the former prison and fort that now houses the Constitutional Court: open 9am to 5pm daily per its own site; guided tours of the Old Fort and Women's Jail can be booked through the site

days.title: Soweto
activities: Hector Pieterson Memorial and Museum, Khumalo Street, Orlando West, on the 1976 student uprising. City of Johannesburg pages disagree on opening days (one lists Monday to Saturday, a May 2024 article Tuesday to Sunday), so confirm before you go.
Vilakazi Street in Orlando West, where Nelson Mandela's former home is a museum; check its hours and book a guide in advance
Many visitors join a guided Soweto tour; use a guide who is registered and booked in advance

days.title: Fly to Kruger: Skukuza
activities: Airlink flight from OR Tambo to Skukuza Airport, about 1 hour (Airlink's Skukuza airport page lists daily departures at 10:05 and 13:05; confirm when booking). The alternative is a long road trip on the N4 to a Kruger gate; check a live map for distance and time.
Collect a rental car (Airlink's Skukuza airport page lists Avis Budget as car hire at the airport, with an Avis shuttle to the main camp) and check in at Skukuza Rest Camp

Complete the Gate Registration & Indemnity Form and have your passport ready. Camp and entrance gates close at night: SANParks gives 17:30 to 18:30 depending on the month, so be in your camp before closing.
Late-afternoon self-drive on the tourist roads near the camp
days.drive_time: Flight OR Tambo to Skukuza, ~1 hr (Airlink: 10:05 to 11:05 or 13:05 to 14:05)

days.title: Skukuza to Lower Sabie
activities: Start at gate-opening time: camp gates open 04:30 to 06:00 depending on the month, and entrance gates 05:30 to 06:00 (SANParks)

Self-drive toward Lower Sabie. Speed limits are 50 km/h on tarred roads, 40 km/h on gravel and 20 km/h in rest camps; SANParks recommends an average of about 30 km/h for safety and game viewing. Sable Dam Hide is one of the activities SANParks lists.
Check in to Lower Sabie Rest Camp before the gates close
days.drive_time: Lower Sabie is 1 hr from Crocodile Bridge gate and 1 hr 30 from Paul Kruger gate at minimum legal speeds (SANParks)

days.title: Lower Sabie full day
activities: Full day of self-drive around Lower Sabie. Kruger's mammal list includes the Big Five (buffalo, elephant, leopard, lion, rhino) per SANParks; no sighting is guaranteed.
Book a guided game drive through SANParks (listed under Kruger activities), which is the way to see the park at night or at dawn
Bush braai or a camp meal; SANParks also lists Bush Braais & Breakfasts as an activity

days.title: Back to Skukuza
activities: Slow morning drive back to Skukuza (allow the whole morning; no official time is published for this leg, and the average speed on tourist roads is about 30 km/h)
Skukuza is the park's main camp and sits close to the airport; check SANParks for current facilities such as medical help and pool access when you book
Early night before the flight

days.title: Fly back to Johannesburg
activities: Return rental car, then Airlink Skukuza to OR Tambo (Airlink's Skukuza airport page lists daily departures at 13:35 and 14:35; confirm on the Airlink site)
Connect to your onward flight from OR Tambo, leaving a generous margin after the flight
days.drive_time: Flight Skukuza to OR Tambo, about 1 hr (Airlink: 13:35 to 14:40 or 14:35 to 15:40)

food_culture.name: The braai
food_culture.description: The South African barbecue is a social tradition; SANParks even lists Bush Braais & Breakfasts among Kruger's activities.

food_culture.name: Boerewors and pap
food_culture.description: Coiled spiced sausage grilled over a fire, served with maize-meal porridge (pap), a staple of braais and township eateries.

food_culture.name: Biltong
food_culture.description: Air-dried cured meat sold across South Africa, including in Kruger camp shops and at roadside stops.

food_culture.name: Soweto
food_culture.description: South Africa's best-known township, tied to the 1976 student uprising remembered at the Hector Pieterson Memorial and Museum.

food_culture.name: Rooibos tea
food_culture.description: A caffeine-free herbal tea made from a plant grown in the Western Cape, widely served across South Africa.

title: Seoul, DMZ, Gyeongju + Busan, South Korea
best_time_description: Spring and early autumn suit this city-and-train route. VisitKorea's 2026 cherry blossom forecast gave first bloom around 25 March in Busan, 28 March in Gyeongju and 3 April in Seoul, with peak about a week after first bloom; dates shift every year, so check the current forecast. VisitKorea says June to October is also typhoon season and that the rainy season overlaps late June to late July, so check forecasts if you travel then. Winters are cold, often below freezing. Several sights close one weekday (Gyeongbokgung on Tuesdays, the DMZ sites on Mondays), so order the days around that.
description: A classic first trip to South Korea by rail: two days in Seoul, a guided DMZ day, the KTX south to Gyeongju, the former Silla capital, then on to Busan on the coast, with a KTX back to Seoul.

days.title: Arrive Seoul + Gyeongbokgung Palace
activities: Check in and settle into central Seoul

Gyeongbokgung Palace: closed every Tuesday (if a public holiday falls on a Tuesday the palace opens and the closure moves to the next non-holiday), with seasonal opening hours listed on royalpalace.go.kr, so check the hours for your month. Visit Seoul says entry is free if you wear a hanbok.
Changing of the Royal Guard at the palace, listed by VisitKorea at 10:00 and 14:00 and not held on Tuesdays; confirm the day's schedule before going

days.title: Seoul old and new
activities: Bukchon Hanok Village and the lanes around Insadong
Gwangjang Market for a street-food lunch
Evening at Namsan and N Seoul Tower

days.title: DMZ guided tour from Seoul
activities: Guided DMZ tour: Dora Observatory is reachable only on a reserved guided DMZ Peace Tour departing from Imjingak, and individual visits are not allowed. Book ahead through the official channels or a licensed tour operator.
Bring your passport: VisitKorea says all visitors must bring ID such as a passport

The Third Tunnel: VisitKorea lists it as needing advance reservation and closed Mondays, weekday public holidays, Seollal and Chuseok; VisitKorea lists the Dora Observatory as closed Mondays. Do not plan this day for a Monday.
Return to Seoul in the evening
days.drive_time: Guided tour from Imjingak; tour operators set the schedule, so confirm the pick-up and return times when you book

days.title: KTX to Gyeongju
activities: KTX from Seoul Station to Singyeongju Station, about 2 hours 10 minutes per the Gyeongju city website (trains roughly hourly from Seoul, first 07:37 and last 00:07 per that page; check korail.com for the day's timetable)
Singyeongju Station is outside central Gyeongju, so allow for a bus or taxi into town
Evening walk among the tumuli of Daereungwon and Cheomseongdae observatory
days.drive_time: KTX Seoul to Singyeongju, ~2 hr 10 min

days.title: Gyeongju: Silla heritage
activities: Bulguksa Temple and Seokguram Grotto on Mt Toham
Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond
Gyeongju National Museum, for Silla-era collections

days.title: KTX to Busan
activities: Return to Singyeongju Station and take the KTX to Busan, about 30 minutes per the Gyeongju city website
Haeundae Beach and the Dongbaek Island promenade
Seafood dinner near Haeundae

days.title: Busan: Gamcheon, Jagalchi, Haedong Yonggungsa
activities: Gamcheon Culture Village, a hillside neighbourhood of painted houses
Jagalchi Market, Busan's waterfront seafood market
Haedong Yonggungsa, a seaside temple on the east coast

days.title: Busan to Seoul + depart
activities: KTX from Busan Station to Seoul Station: Visit Seoul gives about 2 hours 18 minutes for the fastest KTX and VisitKorea guides give about 3 hours, so the running time depends on the train; check the exact time on korail.com for yours
Connect to Incheon or Gimpo airport for departure, leaving a generous buffer for the rail leg
days.drive_time: KTX Busan to Seoul, about 2 hr 20 min to 3 hr depending on the train (Visit Seoul, VisitKorea; check Korail)

food_culture.name: Kimjang, making and sharing kimchi
food_culture.description: UNESCO inscribed Kimjang on its Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2013; the committee describes late autumn as the season when communities make and share large quantities of kimchi.

food_culture.name: Palace visits in hanbok
food_culture.description: Visit Seoul says admission to Gyeongbokgung is free if you enter wearing a hanbok, the traditional Korean dress.

food_culture.name: Fresh seafood at Jagalchi Market
food_culture.description: Busan's Jagalchi Market is a waterfront seafood market, where fish and shellfish are sold and can be eaten in the market's restaurants.

food_culture.name: Silla royal heritage in Gyeongju
food_culture.description: Gyeongju was the capital of the Silla kingdom, and the tumuli, temples and palace ponds in the city are the setting for the day-two sightseeing.

title: Jeju Island + Jeonju, South Korea
best_time_description: Late March to May and October suit Jeju's coast and Hallasan. VisitKorea's 2026 cherry blossom forecast put first bloom on Jeju around 25 March, the earliest in the country. VisitKorea says June to October is typhoon season and the rainy season overlaps late June to late July, so flights and Hallasan trails can be disrupted; the Hallasan trail pages say trails can be restricted at short notice in severe weather. Hallasan's summit entry cut-off is earlier in the winter season (October to March: 11:30 at Seongpanak) than in summer (April to September: 12:30), so an October climb needs the earlier start.
description: Jeju Island's volcanic east coast, a reserved Hallasan summit climb and lava-tube landscapes, then a flight back to Seoul and a KTX south to Jeonju's hanok village and bibimbap.

days.title: Fly Seoul to Jeju
activities: Flight from Seoul to Jeju: VisitKorea calls the Gimpo to Jeju route the busiest in the world, and says direct Incheon to Jeju flights resumed on 12 May 2026 with a flight time of about 1 hour 15 minutes. Check the airline timetable for the day you fly, as the Incheon route has run only on a few days a week.
Jeju International Airport is close to downtown, with city buses to the Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal per VisitKorea; check the current bus timetable
Evening in Jeju City
days.drive_time: Seoul to Jeju flight, ~1 hr 15 min on the Incheon route (VisitKorea)

days.title: East Jeju: Seongsan Ilchulbong
activities: Seongsan Ilchulbong, the volcanic tuff cone on the east coast, part of the UNESCO site Jeju Volcanic Island and Lava Tubes; visitjeju.net says the summit area is closed on the first Monday of every month
Coastal walk along the east shore
Early night before the Hallasan climb

days.title: Hallasan summit via the Seongpanak Trail
activities: A reservation is required for the summit sections, booked in advance on the Hallasan reservation site visithalla.jeju.go.kr; visitjeju.net gives daily limits of 1,000 on Seongpanak and 500 on Gwaneumsa under normal operations, so book early
Seongpanak Trail: 9.6 km one way, about 4 hours 30 minutes up and about 9 hours round trip per the Jeju trail page; the trail opens at 05:00

Summit entry cut-off at the Seongpanak entrance and Jindallaebat checkpoint: 12:30 from April to September and 11:30 from October to March, and the summit must be left by 14:30 in summer or 13:30 in winter (Jeju trail page; the reservation site lists the current table, so check it)
The summit is 1,950 m; the Eorimok, Yeongsil and Donnaeko trails do not reach the Baengnokdam summit (Eorimok ends at Witseoreum, about 1,700 m); the trail can close in severe weather
The Gwaneumsa Trail is the other summit route; its Samgakbong to Baengnokdam section was closed 1 August to 30 September 2026 for rockfall-prevention works

days.title: Lava tubes + coast
activities: Manjanggul lava tube, part of the UNESCO Jeju Volcanic Island and Lava Tubes site; check visitjeju.net for the current opening status before you go
Slow day on the coast after the climb
Look into Jeju's haenyeo (women divers) culture, which UNESCO inscribed in 2016; visitjeju.net lists where it can be seen

days.title: Jeju to Seoul to Jeonju
activities: Morning flight Jeju to Seoul (Gimpo or Incheon), allowing time for the transfer to Yongsan Station

KTX from Yongsan Station to Jeonju Station, about 1 hour 40 minutes per the Jeonju tourism site, which says Yongsan has more frequent KTX departures to Jeonju than Seoul Station; weekend and holiday seats sell out, so reserve early
Evening in Jeonju
days.drive_time: Flight to Seoul, then KTX Yongsan to Jeonju, ~1 hr 40 min

days.title: Jeonju Hanok Village
activities: From Jeonju Station, a taxi to the hanok village takes about 20 minutes (VisitKorea) and the city bus about 25 minutes (Jeonju city guide)
Walk the hanok village; the streets are closed to traffic at weekends, so you must get off on the outskirts and walk in
Gaengnidan Street and a Jeonju bibimbap meal

days.title: Jeonju to Seoul + depart
activities: KTX from Jeonju Station to Yongsan Station, about 1 hour 40 minutes
Transfer to your departure airport, leaving a generous buffer
days.drive_time: KTX Jeonju to Yongsan, ~1 hr 40 min

food_culture.name: Jeju haenyeo, the women divers
food_culture.description: UNESCO inscribed the Culture of Jeju Haenyeo (women divers) on its Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2016; the divers gather shellfish such as abalone and sea urchin without oxygen masks.

food_culture.name: Jeonju bibimbap
food_culture.description: Bibimbap, rice topped with seasoned vegetables and other toppings, is the dish most associated with Jeonju and is served in the restaurants around the hanok village.

food_culture.name: Jeonju Hanok Village
food_culture.description: A district of traditional Korean houses (hanok) in Jeonju; the city says the streets are closed to traffic at weekends.
